# AUDIT-12 — the whole project

AUDIT_HEAD `f9d3089` · run 2026-10-07 → 2026-10-13 · workflow runs W1 `wf_b6f9f068-9ec`, W2 `wf_daf9aa00-415`, W3 `wf_e45d8da9-e9b`, W4 `wf_824197f1-472`, W5 `wf_4c13af57-cb6`, leftover verification `wf_ad7d5217-b36` · step M and the §5.6 re-verify ran as single agents.

Read-only audit (PLAN-12). Nothing under `src/`, `public/`, `admin/` or `data/` was changed. The one other commit on this branch removed a bcrypt-shaped literal from `_harness/invariants-selftest.js` at the owner's instruction (§8).

## 0. Verdict

**Not launch-ready yet: 0 Blocker, but 9 High findings are not yet owned.** Every High reproduced again on a fresh clone at `f9d3089` (§5.6, 9/9). Four are code defects (an interrupted password change empties the password file, replacing a data sheet keeps no backup, ISO text stays in search snippets after Rick clears it, and the link-share card says "Ships same day"); three are wrong or unbacked product and company claims that only Rick can settle, one is a test suite that cannot catch the defect it guards, and one (A12-L3-W5-G2-2) is a deploy-day decision about the old site's admin at `/site/admin/`. That one becomes a **Blocker** if the old admin still accepts the password whose hash is in this public repository's history; that could not be measured, because the plan forbids signing in to the live host. Coverage is complete except for 238 blocked rows (§2, §6); 231 of those are work W5 routed but never ran, because the owner closed W5 on 2026-10-12.

#### A12-L3-W5-G2-2 — High (author: Medium) · decision · L3

**The deploy's password rotation only protects the NEW admin: the old site's admin at /site/admin/, the dashboard the publicly leaked password hash was written about, stays on the server untouched through the whole deploy and afterwards, and the runbook never says to change its password, lock it or take it down before the new site goes live**

- **Rows:** DOC-0026
- **Where:** `GO-LIVE.md:81` · `audit-runs/WHATS_LEFT-history.md:4397` · `WHATS_LEFT.md:86` · `audit-runs/live-triage-2026-09-15.md:59` · `GO-LIVE.md:146` · `GO-LIVE.md:325` · `GO-LIVE.md:521`
- **Reproduce:** On any checkout at f9d3089: bash _harness/out/audit12/findings/A12-L3-W5-G2-2.repro.sh  (read-only greps, no network). It prints (1) the repo history's own statement that the leaked hash was the live dashboard's and that anyone who read the repo could sign in; (2) the settled decision that the password set at deploy (GO-LIVE B4, which writes public_html/admin/config.local.php) is the rotation; (3) the measured existence of /site/admin/ on the live host and GO-LIVE's instruction to sign into it; (4) that /site/ is kept until after C and is the first-deploy rollback; (5) a search of GO-LIVE.md, README.md, WHATS_LEFT.md and admin/README.md for any step that rotates, locks, renames or deletes /site/admin — none.
- **Observed:** _harness/out/audit12/findings/A12-L3-W5-G2-2.repro.out — WHATS_LEFT-history.md:663/788 call the leaked hash 'the live production hash' and :4397 says 'anyone who has read this repository can sign in to the dashboard'; WHATS_LEFT.md:86 settles that 'the password set at deploy is the rotation'; GO-LIVE B4 sets that password in public_html/admin/ only; live-triage:59 measured /site/admin/ answering 302 on 2026-09-15 and GO-LIVE:146 tells the owner to sign into it; GO-LIVE:315-325 keeps public_html/site/ until after C and :521 makes it the rollback; step 5 of the script finds no instruction anywhere to rotate, lock or remove /site/admin. [UNVERIFIED — PLAN-12 S5 forbids signing in to or probing the live host] whether /site/admin/config(.local).php still holds one of the two hashes committed to this public repo (169c0d7 2026-07-07, 1d57237 2026-08-12) and whether that admin generation carries the upload and throttle hardening added since (DEP-3, SEC-1, NB14 etc.).
- **Expected:** The rotation the §1an decision relies on has to cover every admin on the account that a leaked credential could open, before the new site is announced: either B2 (or §A) disables /site/admin/ (rename the folder, or an .htaccess deny) in the same session as B2.0, or the runbook states that /site/admin/ was confirmed to hold no credential from git history. Keagan's call which; it is a decision because it touches the settled §1an rotation and the B2.10/rollback timing.
- **Consequence:** If the predecessor's admin still accepts the credential whose hash has been public since 2026-07-07 (the repo's own history says that was the live dashboard's), anyone who has read this repo can sign in to an admin on the same hosting account for the whole deploy day and for as long as /site/ is kept as the rollback, while the owner believes B4 closed that door. From there they can at least rewrite the predecessor's catalog, which is exactly what visitors see if the rollback is used, and use whatever upload checks that older admin has. Medium, not High, only because whether the predecessor actually accepts a leaked hash is unmeasured from here; if C confirms it does, this is a Blocker (unauthenticated write).
- **Not in prior:** Grepped WHATS_LEFT.md, plans/GUARDRAILS.md §7.x, audit-runs/*.md (WHATS_LEFT-history §1an/§2j/§1o, live-triage, audit-2026-09-27 NEW-V4-1/-3/-8, DEP-6, DEP-13), _harness/AUDIT10-REPORT.md, _harness/AUDIT11-REPORT.md and every _harness/out/audit12 findings/verdict JSON for 'site/admin', 'predecessor', 'rotation', 'is the rotation'. §1an settles NOT rewriting history and names B4 as the rotation; it does not consider that B4 writes a different admin from the one on the live host. DEP-13 (withdrawn) was about the commit id, not the second admin. NEW-V4-3/B2.10 treat /site/ only as a content-loss and broken-copy problem. The L12/L14 W5-G2 items on /site/ are about the redirect and rollback mechanics, not the admin credential. Not in the already-raised L3 list.
- **Verification:** reproduce: confirmed · refute: confirmed · severity: confirmed (High)

<a id="a12-l4-w2-g4-2"></a>
#### A12-L4-W2-G4-2 — High · code · L4

**If a password change is cut off mid-save, the admin password file is left empty; the documented ALLOW-PASSWORD-RESET recovery then says it worked, but nobody can sign in and every admin page, including the public sign-in page, prints the new password hash as plain text**

- **Rows:** DECL-0226, ADMIN-0069, ADMIN-0015
- **Where:** `admin/config.php:190` · `admin/config.php:162` · `admin/config.php:55` · `admin/auth.php:91`
- **Reproduce:** Script: bash _harness/out/audit12/A12-L4-W2-G4-2.repro.sh (repo root; needs strace; private mirror, port 10885; output _harness/out/audit12/A12-L4-W2-G4-2.repro.out). Cold, by hand: 1) cp -r _harness/site M; php -S 127.0.0.1:10885 -t M -c _harness/php-mail.ini _harness/router.php. 2) Sign in (audit-pass-123), open admin/password.php, note csrf_token. 3) Restart the same server under `strace -f -P M/admin/config.local.php -e trace=ftruncate,write -e inject=write:signal=SIGKILL:when=1` (kills the worker at the moment admin_password_write() writes the file — the stand-in for a host kill/timeout/restart in that window) and POST password.php with current_password, new_password=confirm_password='Interrupted-Change-2026!'. 4) Restart normally; `wc -c M/admin/config.local.php` -> 0; sign in with old and new password -> both 200 (refused). 5) Follow the documented recovery: touch M/admin/ALLOW-PASSWORD-RESET; GET auth.php for csrf_token; POST auth.php set_password=1, new_password=confirm_password='Recovered-Password-2026!'. 6) head M/admin/config.local.php; sign in with the recovered password; curl -D- M/admin/auth.php signed out.
- **Observed:** strace: `ftruncate(8, 0) = 0` then `write(8, "<?php\n// TEST HARNESS CREDENTIAL"..., 244) = ?` (killed). config.local.php before 244 bytes starting '<?php'; after 0 bytes (3 .bak copies exist). Sign in with old password -> 200, new -> 200 (neither works); login page points at ALLOW-PASSWORD-RESET. Recovery POST -> 302 to index.php; ALLOW-PASSWORD-RESET deleted; audit log 'Admin password set via FTP-unlocked recovery'. config.local.php is now 146 bytes with NO '<?php' (contains '<?php': 0): two blank lines, '// Added by the IPC admin on 2026-10-09 17:10:29', "define('ADMIN_PASSWORD_HASH', '$2y$12$<HASH REDACTED>');". Sign in with the recovered password -> 200 (refused). Unauthenticated GET admin/auth.php: body begins with that comment and the define line — 'body contains a bcrypt hash: 1' — 'Set-Cookie header sent: 0', and PHP warns 'headers already sent by (output started at .../config.local.php'. Full log: _harness/out/audit12/A12-L4-W2-G4-2.repro.out (hash redacted there).
- **Expected:** The password file is written the way every data file is (json_write_atomic(): temp file + rename, A-5.5), so an interrupted change leaves the old file whole; and admin_password_write() must never produce a config.local.php without an opening '<?php' — an existing file with no tag (empty included) must be rebuilt from the template at line 164, not appended to. The read-back check at :202 should verify the file actually defines the hash when included, not only that the text is present. The code's own promise (config.php:39 'fails CLOSED (nobody can sign in)' with ALLOW-PASSWORD-RESET as the recovery, auth.php:69-75) requires the recovery to actually recover.
- **Consequence:** Rick is locked out of his admin and the one documented self-service recovery (help.php:325, :1180, admin/README.md:391, GO-LIVE B4) reports success while leaving him locked out; repeating it loops (the define is replaced in the same tagless file). Only someone who knows to FTP-edit or delete config.local.php can fix it. Meanwhile every admin URL, including the unauthenticated sign-in page, publishes the admin password's bcrypt hash to anyone, which invites offline cracking of the password that guards the whole catalog and leads inbox. Trigger is narrow (a host kill, timeout or restart between truncate and write, or any empty config.local.php) but the result is a blocked owner plus a credential exposure.
- **Not in prior:** Grepped WHATS_LEFT.md, plans/GUARDRAILS.md (§7*), CLAUDE.md invariants 1-2, audit-runs/*.md incl. WHATS_LEFT-history.md, _harness/AUDIT10-REPORT.md, _harness/AUDIT11-REPORT.md and every _harness/out/audit12/findings/*.json for 'config.local', 'empty config.local', 'open tag', 'rtrim($newBody)', 'admin_password_write'. Hits: invariant 1 (preg_replace_callback — not this), audit5 'either quote style' fix (the appended-define path — not the missing tag), L11 restore-message fix (different branch, never reached here because the read-back passes), A12-L3-09-1 (array field warning on the recovery form — not this), A12-L13-W1-R2-1-2 (default password check — not this). None covers a non-atomic password write or a recovery that writes a tagless PHP file.
- **Verification:** reproduce: confirmed · refute: confirmed · severity: confirmed (High)

<a id="a12-l5-w2-g3-1"></a>
#### A12-L5-W2-G3-1 — High · code · L5

**If Rick stops claiming ISO and, as Business Details tells him, clears or removes the Homepage or About search description, Google and every shared link still say "ISO 9001 registered" (and "$50 minimum order", "Bolingbrook") from built-in text — while the admin's ISO warning reports those entries gone**

- **Rows:** DATA-0067, DATA-0035, DATA-0038
- **Where:** `src/App.jsx:7952` · `src/App.jsx:7949` · `src/App.jsx:7406` · `src/App.jsx:7413` · `public/index.php:542` · `admin/config.php:1212` · `admin/settings.php:359` · `WHATS_LEFT.md:25`
- **Reproduce:** From the repo root with a built mirror (npm run build && sh _harness/sync.sh; php and the harness Playwright available): node _harness/out/audit12/A12-L5-W2-G3-1.repro.js 10864   (any free port >= 10000). It copies _harness/site to _harness/out/audit12/m/A12-L5-W2-G3-1, loads _harness/pristine data, and for six data variants prints, for / and /about, the meta description index.php serves, the description and og:description the hydrated browser ends with, whether the footer still mentions ISO 9001, and what Business Details' ISO warning (iso_mentions() in admin/config.php, run by php -r on the same data) lists for the SEO section; then stops its server and deletes the copy. Variants: control; ISO box emptied; ISO emptied + home/about SEO 'desc' set to ""; ISO emptied + home/about SEO rows removed; minimumOrder $75 + city Naperville + home/about desc ""; minimumOrder $75 + city Naperville with the stored rows kept. Admin path: Business Details -> ISO box cleared -> Save (the warning lists 'Search Engine Text (SEO) (row 1)' and '(row 6)'); Page Content -> Search Engine Text (SEO) -> empty the Meta description of the home and about rows (content.php keeps a row with a title and saves desc ""), or empty both fields so content.php drops the row as fully blank -> Save.
- **Observed:** _harness/out/audit12/A12-L5-W2-G3-1.repro.out. 'ISO box emptied only': footer mentions ISO 9001: false; iso_mentions() lists 2 SEO entries (rows 1 and 6). 'ISO emptied + home & about SEO desc blanked' and '... rows removed': iso_mentions(): 8 entries, SEO entries: [] — yet / serves index.php description AND browser description AND og:description "IPC is a spec-grade stocking distributor of heat-shrinkable & extruded tubing, electrical sleeving, and industrial adhesives. $50 minimum order. ISO 9001 registered." and /about serves "Insulation Products Corporation — a spec-grade stocking distributor in Bolingbrook, IL since July 1, 1974. ISO 9001 registered. $50 minimum order." in all three. 'min order $75, city Naperville, stored rows kept': both renderers say "$75 minimum order" and "Naperville, IL" (the ADM-7 waterfall reaches stored rows). 'min order $75, city Naperville + desc blanked': both renderers revert to "$50 minimum order" and "Bolingbrook, IL". The two renderers agree in every variant; the defect is the shared fallback: SEO_DEFAULT (App.jsx 7406/7413, ported to index.php ipc_seo_default) is used whenever a stored row has no description, and it goes through localizeProse only — neither withIsoLabel/isoRewriter nor factsRewriter (ContentProvider rewrites the stored content tree, not SEO_DEFAULT), and iso_mentions() scans only stored content, so the admin cannot see it.
- **Expected:** §1aq (WHATS_LEFT line 25, history §1aq): an empty ISO box means the site stops claiming ISO, and Business Details lists every place that still does. ADM-7 (history §1ae): hours, founded year, city, minimum order and feet in stock come from their one Business Details field 'every content section, SEO included'. A description the owner cleared or removed must not be replaced by built-in text carrying an ISO claim or stale business facts that his own warning list no longer shows — either the fallback goes through the same isoRewriter/factsRewriter chokepoint (and an empty ISO source drops the ISO sentence), or a cleared description stays empty/falls back to text without such claims, and iso_mentions() covers whatever text can still be served.
- **Consequence:** The day IPC's registration lapses and Rick follows the admin's own instructions (clear the ISO box, then edit or remove each listed entry), the homepage and About search snippets and every LinkedIn/Teams share card keep asserting 'ISO 9001 registered' — a certification claim the business can no longer stand behind, to aerospace/medical/automotive buyers who check — and the admin's ISO warning shows nothing left to fix, so he has no way to find it. Today, without the ISO change, clearing either description after changing the minimum order or moving the city makes search results quote the old '$50 minimum order' and 'Bolingbrook, IL' while the site says otherwise. High: a claim the business cannot stand behind, on the main discovery path, with a control (the ISO warning list) that fails silently.
- **Not in prior:** Grepped WHATS_LEFT.md, plans/GUARDRAILS.md, audit-runs/*.md (incl. WHATS_LEFT-history §1aq, §1ae ADM-7, B25), _harness/AUDIT10-REPORT.md, AUDIT11-REPORT.md, CLAUDE.md and every _harness/out/audit12/findings/*.json for SEO_DEFAULT, dflt.desc, iso_mentions, 'ISO box is empty', 'ISO 9001 registered'. B25 decided that a route WITHOUT a row falls back to its own default (about which page's text, not about claims). §1aq settled that STORED Page Content wording is left as typed and listed; it records index.html's static share-card text as the one fixed exception, and A-5.10/G3 then made SEO text reach the card. Nothing records SEO_DEFAULT descriptions bypassing the ISO/facts rewrite or iso_mentions(). Differs from A12-L5-05-3 (ISO token regex and '-2015' doubling), A12-L5-02-2 (whitespace-only ISO in footer/About) and A12-L5-04-1 (wrong-type SEO rows) — here both renderers agree and the data is exactly what the admin writes.
- **Verification:** reproduce: confirmed · refute: confirmed · severity: confirmed (High)

**The contact suite's check that a quote request shows safely in the owner's Inquiries page stays green when the page stops escaping what visitors type**

- **Rows:** FILE-0104, FILE-0103
- **Where:** `_harness/contactflow.js:135` · `_harness/contactflow.js:712` · `_harness/contactflow.js:706` · `admin/inquiries.php:206` · `CLAUDE.md:244`
- **Reproduce:** 1. From the repo root with the mirror bootstrapped (sh _harness/sync.sh && php _harness/setpw.php): M=$PWD/_harness/out/audit12/m/repro; mkdir -p $M/tmp; cp -r _harness/site $M/site; cp _harness/contactflow.js _harness/browser.js _harness/fakemail.sh $M/
2. sed -i "s#127.0.0.1:8123#127.0.0.1:10017#" $M/contactflow.js
3. php -S 127.0.0.1:10017 -t $M/site -c _harness/php-mail.ini -d sys_temp_dir=$M/tmp _harness/router.php &
4. Control: node $M/contactflow.js --only=viewer   -> contactflow: 4/4
5. Mutate the copy only: sed -i "s#<?= h(\$e\['special'\]) ?>#<?= \$e['special'] ?>#; s#<small><?= h(\$e\['company'\] ?? '') ?></small>#<small><?= (\$e['company'] ?? '') ?></small>#" $M/site/admin/inquiries.php ; diff admin/inquiries.php $M/site/admin/inquiries.php shows lines 186 and 206 changed.
6. node $M/contactflow.js --only=viewer ; echo $?   -> all four viewer checks ok, contactflow: 4/4, exit 0.
7. Stop the server by PID (ps -eo pid,comm,args, comm==php, :10017) and rm -rf $M.
(Note: contactflow's clearGuards() deletes ipc_rl_/ipc_ar_ files in os.tmpdir(); to avoid touching another server's limiter state, point it at $M/tmp as recorded in the evidence file.)
- **Observed:** With h() removed from the Special reqs cell and the company name in the mirror's admin/inquiries.php, `contactflow.js --only=viewer` prints `ok` for all four viewer checks including "the spec string renders LITERALLY" and "nothing in the lead was parsed as markup", and exits 0 (contactflow: 4/4). Artifact: _harness/out/audit12/evidence/L13-07-contactflow-viewer-mutant.txt. Cause: the fixture `<1/4 inch and >2 inch ID` and `O'Brien & Sons` contain no tag-shaped text (`<` is followed by a digit), so the browser shows the same text whether or not it was escaped; the markup check looks for <script|<b>|<i> that the fixture never sends. contactflow-selftest has no mutation for the viewer arm, and invariants.js INV10a/b check only contact.php's s() and hdr(). The one probe that checks the escaped HTML (audit9-logic-contact.js C13, `&lt;1/4 inch`) is an instrument, not in sweep-list.txt.
- **Expected:** Invariant 10 (CLAUDE.md) puts escaping at the render boundary, h() in inquiries.php. The suite says that this arm checks that boundary ("has to arrive here as literal text, not as markup"), so it must go red when h() is removed. For example, it could send a tag-shaped value such as `<b>x</b>` and assert that the escaped text appears, or assert `&lt;` in the raw response.
- **Consequence:** inquiries.php shows text that anyone on the internet typed into the public contact form, and it shows it inside the owner's signed-in admin session. If an edit drops one h() call there, that becomes stored XSS in the admin. The sweep would stay all-green, because the only sweep suite that claims to guard this boundary cannot fail. That makes it a security control that would fail silently, guarded by a suite that cannot fail while it guards an invariant (§9.2 High).
- **Not in prior:** Grepped WHATS_LEFT.md, plans/GUARDRAILS.md, _harness/AUDIT10-REPORT.md, _harness/AUDIT11-REPORT.md, audit-runs/audit*.md and audit-runs/WHATS_LEFT-history.md for 'parsed as markup', 'viewer arm', '--only=viewer' and 'contactflow'. audit3.md:45 covers a different defect: the viewer block cascaded red when a fixture 422'd, which has been fixed. WHATS_LEFT-history.md:1889 records a DOM observation, not this test. Nothing records that the viewer arm cannot detect h() being removed.
- **Verification:** reproduce: confirmed · refute: confirmed · severity: confirmed (High)

#### A12-L2-01-1 — Medium · code · L2

**A product photo Rick deletes or removes stays downloadable on the public site, although the code and the admin README say trashed files are hidden from the web**

- **Rows:** FILE-0505, FILE-0431
- **Where:** `admin/config.php:2471` · `admin/config.php:2472` · `admin/README.md:267` · `uploads/.htaccess:24`
- **Reproduce:** Real Apache 2.4 + mod_php + mod_ssl, docroot = a copy of the mirror with every repo .htaccess. Scripted: `cp -r _harness/site _harness/out/audit12/m/L2-01 && cd _harness/out/audit12/L2-01 && php -r '$i=imagecreatetruecolor(4,4); imagepng($i, "real.png");' && HTTP=<free port> HTTPS=<free port> VARIANT=C node apache-probe.js` (signs in with the mirror's test credential, uploads a PNG for SKU CC on admin/upload-image.php, presses Remove Photo, then GETs /uploads/images/.deleted.CC.png). By hand on any Apache host with the repo's public/.htaccess at the root and uploads/.htaccess in uploads/: 1) Admin → Products → Photo on any product, upload a JPG/PNG; 2) press Remove Photo (or Delete the product); 3) `curl -sk -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code} %{content_type}\n' https://<host>/uploads/images/.deleted.<SKU>.<ext>`. Control: the same for a data sheet, `/pdfs/.deleted.<SKU>.pdf`, answers 403.
- **Observed:** _harness/out/audit12/L2-01/apache-probe-C.txt: `upload alert: Photo uploaded and product updated` → `remove says: Photo removed. The product will show the IPC branded placeholder.` → `trashed files on disk: .deleted.CC.png` → `GET https:/uploads/images/.deleted.CC.png → 200 {Content-Type: image/png | Content-Length: 90}`. Same in apache-probe-A.txt for a planted `.deleted.OLD.png` (200 image/png), while `/pdfs/.deleted.OLD.pdf → 403`. Cause: uploads/.htaccess re-allows every name ending in an image extension (line 24) and, merged after the root's `<FilesMatch "^\.">` deny, that allow wins for dot-prefixed names too; pdfs/ has no allow-list, so its trash stays denied.
- **Expected:** admin/config.php:2471-2473 (ADM-3) and admin/README.md:267/297 promise a trashed `.deleted.<name>` file is kept off the web; a removed photo should answer 403 like a removed data sheet does.
- **Consequence:** Rick removes a wrong, outdated or someone-else's photo (or deletes the product) and is told it is gone; it stays publicly fetchable at a predictable URL (/uploads/images/.deleted.<SKU>.<ext>) indefinitely, since nothing prunes trash. A guarantee written into the code fails silently on a secondary path; nothing is linked to it, so a visitor has to guess the name.
- **Not in prior:** grepped WHATS_LEFT.md, plans/GUARDRAILS.md, audit-runs/*.md, _harness/AUDIT10-REPORT.md, _harness/AUDIT11-REPORT.md and _harness/*.js for `.deleted.`, `trash`, `ADM-3`: ADM-3 (audit-2026-09-27) introduced the trash and asserted the dotfile rule hides it; no suite (dep3-scriptblock.js, lowsE-apache.js, adm3-deleterestore.js) requests a trashed file over Apache. The uploads deny-by-default allow-list (2026-09-29, after ADM-3) is what re-exposes it, so this is new, not a re-raise.

#### A12-L2-W5-G3-1 — Medium · code · L2

**If the host puts the site behind the HTTPS front end that the site's own Apache file is written for, the quote form's '5 per 10 minutes' limit applies to ALL buyers together: the sixth quote request on the whole site in ten minutes is refused, and from the sixteenth on nothing reaches Rick at all (no email, no Inquiries row)**

- **Rows:** HTACCESS-0072, ENDPOINT-0017, DECL-0219
- **Where:** `public/.htaccess:30` · `public/.htaccess:52` · `public/contact.php:564` · `public/contact.php:569` · `public/contact.php:570` · `public/contact.php:661` · `admin/config.php:1672` · 17 different buyers, one RFQ each, through an Apache mod_proxy_http front end to the Apache 2.4 + mod_php origin (port 10861/10862, HEAD f2152f4) (artifact `_harness/out/audit12/L2-W5-G3x/proxy-ratelimit.out`)
- **Reproduce:** From the repo root, on a machine with Apache 2.4 (/usr/sbin/apache2, modules in /usr/lib/apache2/modules incl. mod_proxy, mod_proxy_http, libphp8.3.so) and node:
  bash _harness/out/audit12/L2-W5-G3x/proxy-ratelimit.sh 10861
The script copies _harness/site into _harness/out/audit12/m/L2-W5-G3x-proxy, starts an origin Apache with mod_php on 10861 (public/.htaccess verbatim, private sys_temp_dir and capturing sendmail via php_admin_value) and a second Apache on 10862 acting as the TLS-terminating front end (ProxyPass + RequestHeader X-Forwarded-Proto https; mod_proxy_http appends X-Forwarded-For). Each buyer is a different client source address (curl --interface 127.0.0.N) sending ONE ordinary RFQ. A) control: 7 buyers straight to the origin. B) 17 buyers through the front end. It prints status codes, mails captured, inquiry rows by status/ip and the buyers with no row, then stops both Apaches and deletes the copy.
- **Observed:** A) CONTROL direct, 7 different buyers: 200 200 200 200 200 200 200
B) THROUGH THE PROXY, 17 different buyers: 200 200 200 200 200 429 429 429 429 429 429 429 429 429 429 429 429
last response body: {"ok":false,"error":"Too many submissions. Please try again in a few minutes, or call 630.771.0700 directly."}
limiter files in temp dir: 1
sales notifications mailed: 5
inquiry rows: 15  { 'rfq ip=127.0.0.1': 5, 'rate-limited ip=127.0.0.1': 10 }
buyers with NO row at all: B36 B37
origin error log PHP lines: 0
(also: every row, accepted or refused, records the front end's address 127.0.0.1, not the buyer's.) grep -n FORWARDED public/contact.php -> no hits; the admin sign-in throttle has a TRUST_PROXY_FORWARDED switch for exactly this topology (admin/config.php:1667-1684), contact.php has none.
- **Expected:** public/.htaccess ships for two topologies and says the proxy one is common ('it often does not' terminate TLS on this server; the X-Forwarded-Proto condition 'is not optional'). In that topology every request's REMOTE_ADDR is the front end's, so a limit meant as 'per buyer' must key on the client address the trusted front end reports, or at least be switchable the way login_throttle_client_ip() is. The limiter's own comment says it is per-IP so that one office does not crowd out others; behind a proxy it is per-site.
- **Consequence:** Only on a host that fronts PHP with a TLS-terminating proxy or CDN [UNVERIFIED for Network Solutions: no access to the production host (S5); the repo records no measurement of its topology]. There, the whole site gets 5 quote/contact submissions per 10 minutes. Buyers 6-15 in a window see 'Too many submissions' (with the phone number) and Rick gets only a 'rate-limited, no email was sent' row; from buyer 16 on, the lead leaves no trace anywhere. Honeypot spam and a phone buyer's own retries on a dropping connection consume the same shared budget, so one spam bot posting once every two minutes keeps real buyers refused. Workaround exists (the refusal names the phone number), hence Medium, not the Blocker 'lead path fails' it would be for buyers 16+ if the topology is confirmed.
- **Not in prior:** Grepped WHATS_LEFT.md, plans/GUARDRAILS.md, audit-runs/WHATS_LEFT-history.md, audit-runs/audit5..9.md, audit-2026-09-27.md, _harness/AUDIT10/11-REPORT.md and every _harness/out/audit12/findings/*.json title for REMOTE_ADDR, X-Forwarded-For, TRUST_PROXY, proxy, rate limit, NAT, CGNAT. Hits: audit5 refuted the ADMIN throttle being spoofable via XFF (opposite direction); history B3/NB8/A-5.9 moved and logged the limiter but never considered the proxy topology; ledger row ENDPOINT-0017 passed contact.php for ignoring a client-sent XFF (the spoof direction, correct and unchanged here); A12-L3-W2-G1-1 is the IPv6 /64 under-limiting case (one attacker gets unlimited slots) - this is the opposite, over-limiting every legitimate buyer into one slot set. None of the listed already-raised L2 items covers it.
- **Verification:** reproduce: confirmed · refute: confirmed · severity: confirmed (Medium)

#### A12-L3-15-1 — Medium · code · L3

**A quote request or message whose subject line runs long and has an accented letter at the cut-off (or contains one stray non-UTF-8 byte) reaches the sales inbox with a completely empty Subject**

- **Rows:** ENDPOINT-0015, ENDPOINT-0011, ENDPOINT-0005
- **Where:** `public/contact.php:394` · `public/contact.php:385` · `public/contact.php:407` · `public/contact.php:879` · `public/contact.php:798`
- **Reproduce:** From the repo root: bash _harness/out/audit12/A12-L3-15-1.repro.sh <free port, e.g. 10015>  (refuses to run if the port answers; copies _harness/site to a private mirror, serves it with a private capturing sendmail and private sys_temp_dir, POSTs three submissions to /contact.php with curl, prints each sales notification's Subject header, stops the server by PID and deletes the mirror). Case 1 is an ordinary Spanish-language message: name 'José García', subject 'Cotización urgente: tubería aislante térmica para línea de vapor, 2 pulgadas de diámetro, 300 metros, entrega en Querétaro antes del 15 de noviembre — favor de confirmar' (169 characters; the form sets no maxLength). Case 2 is the control with a short accented subject. Case 3 is an RFQ with partNumber=IP12%FFGA.
- **Observed:** _harness/out/audit12/A12-L3-15-1.repro.out: 'real-world subject (169 characters): HTTP 200  sales Subject: []'; 'control, short subject: HTTP 200  sales Subject: [=?UTF-8?B?SVBDIENvbnRhY3QgRm9ybSDigJQgQ290aXphY2nDs24g...]'; 'RFQ part number with byte 0xFF: HTTP 200  sales Subject: []'. Mechanism (measured with php -r): hdr() runs s() over the whole built subject, which cuts it at 200 BYTES with substr(); when that cut lands inside a 2-byte character the string is invalid UTF-8, preg_match_all('/./us') in mime_header() returns false with $m[0] = [], and mime_header() returns ''. Sweeping that subject's length 150..177 chars gave an empty Subject at 5 lengths (155, 162, 168, 169, 170) — run3.py in _harness/out/audit12/L3-15/. The same empty Subject for an invalid byte in name, subject or partNumber (run1.out rows name/rfq/badutf8, name/msg/badutf8, subject/msg/badutf8, partNumber/rfq/badutf8). Side observation from the same run: when the subject is cut but not emptied, the header ends with ' … [truncated — the visitor sent more than 200 characters; please reply and ask for the rest]' and the visitor's name is dropped, although the visitor typed a subject of only 184 bytes (run2.py in _harness/out/audit12/L3-15/). Lead is still mailed (body intact) and logged.
- **Expected:** Every sales notification carries a readable Subject (the PUB-5 fix's purpose: RFC 2047-encode, not drop, non-ASCII). A byte cut must not split a UTF-8 character, and mime_header() must not turn an encoding failure into an empty header.
- **Consequence:** Sales gets the lead with '(no subject)' instead of 'IPC Contact Form — … — José García' / 'IPC Quote Request — <part> — <name>': the notification is easy to miss or file as junk in Rick's inbox, and it is most likely for exactly the non-English, long-subject enquiries. The lead is not lost (body and Inquiries row intact), so Medium (wrong on the main lead path, with the Inquiries page as workaround).
- **Not in prior:** grepped WHATS_LEFT.md, plans/GUARDRAILS.md, audit-runs/*.md (incl. WHATS_LEFT-history.md), _harness/AUDIT10-REPORT.md, _harness/AUDIT11-REPORT.md and _harness/out/audit12/findings/*.json for 'mime_header', 'PUB-5', 'empty subject', 'blank subject', 'truncat.*subject', 'invalid utf-8', 'straddl'. PUB-5 (audit-2026-09-27.md:106, fixed §1af, lowsB-contact.js) added the encoding; nothing records that a byte-split or invalid byte empties the header. A-5.24 / NB6 cover invalid UTF-8 in json_encode and preg_replace, not mime_header().
- **Verification:** reproduce: confirmed · refute: confirmed · severity: confirmed (Medium)

#### A12-L3-W2-G1-1 — Medium · code · L3

**The contact form's '5 submissions per 10 minutes' limit counts each IPv6 address separately, so one ordinary IPv6 internet connection can send the sales inbox an unlimited number of quote-request emails and grow the inquiry log without end, although the admin sign-in throttle was fixed for exactly this (SEC-6)**

- **Rows:** ENDPOINT-0017, ENDPOINT-0001
- **Where:** `public/contact.php:550` · `public/contact.php:565` · `public/contact.php:566` · `admin/config.php:1693` · `admin/config.php:1697`
- **Reproduce:** From the repo root: sh _harness/out/audit12/L3-W2-G1/repro.sh 10823   (any free port at 10000+). It copies _harness/site to _harness/out/audit12/L3-W2-G1/run/site, serves it with php -S, a private sys_temp_dir and a private capturing sendmail, through the test-only shim _harness/out/audit12/L3-W2-G1/v6router.php, which sets REMOTE_ADDR from an X-Test-Addr header (standing in for what Apache puts there for a real IPv6 client) and then requires the mirror's unmodified contact.php. It POSTs ordinary 'message' submissions: A) 7 from 2001:db8:aa:bb::1; B) then 1 each from 2001:db8:aa:bb::2 .. ::8 (the same /64); C) 7 from the IPv4 address 198.51.100.7 as the control. It prints the HTTP codes and the mails captured, stops the server by PID and deletes the copy.
- **Observed:** _harness/out/audit12/L3-W2-G1/repro.out: 'A) one IPv6 address, 7 submissions: 200 200 200 200 200 429 429'; 'B) 7 other addresses in that same /64 (one customer's allocation), 1 each: 200 200 200 200 200 200 200'; 'C) control, one IPv4 address, 7 submissions: 200 200 200 200 200 429 429'; 'sales notifications mailed: 17'; 'auto-replies mailed: 3' (the per-recipient auto-reply cap holds); 'limiter files: 9' (one per address); 'inquiry rows: 71' (50 in the mirror before, +17 accepted, +4 logged 429s). So the /64 that had already been refused got 7 more submissions through, 12 accepted inside one 10-minute window against a limit of 5; each further address in the /64 (2^64 of them) is a fresh allowance. The key is the full address string (contact.php:564-566); the admin's login throttle collapses IPv6 to its /64 (config.php:1690-1708, SEC-6) and contact.php has no equivalent.
- **Expected:** The contact limiter keys an IPv6 client on its /64, as SEC-6 decided for the sign-in throttle for the same reason ('a single customer is routinely handed a whole /64'), so one connection gets 5 submissions per 10 minutes whichever of its addresses it uses. login_throttle_key() already implements that rule, including the v4-mapped case (SEC-A1).
- **Consequence:** The rate limit is the only thing between an anonymous script and Rick's sales inbox: it is what stops a flood of 'IPC Contact Form / IPC Quote Request' emails, unbounded growth of admin/inquiries.jsonl (whose archives are deliberately never deleted, contact.php:540-541) and the new-inquiries badge being pushed up by junk. From any IPv6 connection it does none of that, and nothing signals it: no log line, no dashboard warning. Not a data exposure and the auto-reply cap still protects third parties, so Medium (a control that degrades without a signal). [UNVERIFIED — whether the Network Solutions host accepts IPv6 connections was not measured: no request to the live host is allowed (§4 S5) and step0.txt records no AAAA lookup. If the site is IPv4-only the gap is latent until the host or a CDN adds IPv6.]
- **Not in prior:** grepped WHATS_LEFT.md, plans/GUARDRAILS.md, audit-runs/*.md (incl. WHATS_LEFT-history.md, audit-2026-09-27.md), _harness/AUDIT10-REPORT.md, _harness/AUDIT11-REPORT.md and _harness/out/audit12/findings/*.json + rows/*.jsonl for 'IPv6', '/64', 'rate limit', 'rate-limit', 'per IP', 'per-IP', '5-per'. Every IPv6 hit is the ADMIN login throttle (SEC-6 at audit-2026-09-27.md:87, SEC-A1, and audit12 rows DECL-0280/0288 for login_throttle_key); none concerns contact.php's limiter. Not one of the already-raised L3 items (the gmail/googlemail auto-reply cap A12-L3-02-2 is the per-RECIPIENT cap, which this run shows still holds; this is the per-SENDER limit). Not settled in WHATS_LEFT 'Settled'.
- **Verification:** reproduce: confirmed · refute: confirmed · severity: confirmed (Medium)

(2) sustained: t=20s, 40s, 61s, 81s, 101s — every correct-password attempt refused ('Please wait about 28 / 7 / 47 / 27 / 7 seconds'), 201 forged POSTs sent; throttle record c=8 at the end. The screenshot lockout-sustained.png (opened) shows the Sign In card with 'Please wait about 7 seconds' — 7 seconds after which the background tab re-arms the window again.
- **Expected:** A sign-in attempt that a browser marks as coming from another website (Sec-Fetch-Site: cross-site / same-site, or an Origin that is not this host) should be refused before it reaches login_attempt_gate(), so only attempts made from the admin's own sign-in page count. The admin already applies this rule for the same SameSite=Lax reason on the Inquiries page (SEC-10, admin/inquiries.php reads HTTP_SEC_FETCH_SITE). The throttle's own stated rule is that 'Rick must never be stranded' (config.php LOGIN_COOLOFF_MAX comment) and that a refused attempt does not extend the wait — both assume every counted attempt is someone actually typing.
- **Consequence:** Rick is blocked from the whole admin (every product, content, inquiry and password screen) for as long as a page on any other site is open in any tab of any browser on his network address — a link in an email, an ad, a compromised supplier site — and a coworker's browser behind the same office connection does it equally. The message tells him the block 'clears itself' in a few seconds, so he retries and waits indefinitely; FTP recovery does not help (the cool-off is checked before the password). The Audit Log fills with 'Incorrect password … failure #N from this address' rows showing his own IP and browser, pointing him at himself. No data is exposed or changed; the remedy is closing the right tab, which nothing tells him to do. Medium: Rick blocked on his main path, but it needs him to have a hostile page open and the attacker gains nothing but the denial.
- **Not in prior:** Grepped WHATS_LEFT.md, plans/GUARDRAILS.md, CLAUDE.md, audit-runs/*.md (incl. WHATS_LEFT-history.md), _harness/AUDIT10-REPORT.md, _harness/AUDIT11-REPORT.md and _harness/out/audit12/findings/*.json for 'login csrf', 'lockout', 'locked out', 'lock him out', 'cross-site', 'Sec-Fetch', 'throttle', 'per-IP', 'cool-off'. Hits: D14/4.14 (throttle is per-IP, so a DISTRIBUTED attacker is unaffected — the opposite direction), SEC-6 (IPv6 /64 keying), SEC-A2 (X-Forwarded-For), NEW-N3-10 (docs say 'after 5'), SEC-10 (Inquiries cross-site GET clears the badge — same Lax mechanism, different page), history line 4036 (Help wording of the lockout), and this wave's A12-L3-06-1 (throttle file unwritable -> no throttle at all). None covers forged cross-site sign-in attempts being counted against the owner's own address. The posture paragraph's 'csrf_check() on every mutating POST (login excepted)' records the login exception for CSRF tokens; this is not a request to put a token on the login form but that the login POST's side effect (the throttle) is reachable cross-site.
- **Verification:** reproduce: confirmed · refute: confirmed · severity: confirmed (Medium)

<a id="a12-l3-w2-g3-1"></a>
#### A12-L3-W2-G3-1 — Medium · code · L3

**The contact form's limit of 3 auto-replies a day to one mailbox can be skipped for ANY address by writing it in quotes ("joe"@example.com, "\joe"@example.com, ...), so one IP can make IPC's domain send a stranger hundreds of confirmation emails a day instead of 3**

- **Rows:** FILE-0433, ENDPOINT-0013
- **Where:** `public/contact.php:838` · `public/contact.php:483` · `public/contact.php:496` · `public/contact.php:509` · `public/contact.php:955` · `public/contact.php:957`
- **Reproduce:** Port 10862 by default (override with PORT=<free port>). Copy kept at _harness/out/audit12/evidence/L3-W2-G3/repro1.sh; run `bash _harness/out/audit12/evidence/L3-W2-G3/repro1.sh` from inside the repo. It copies _harness/site into a private mirror, serves it with php -S under _harness/php-mail.ini (fakemail sendmail) with a private sys_temp_dir and IPC_MAIL_LOG, posts the message form 8 times with email = joe@example.com, "joe"@example.com, "\joe"@example.com, "j\oe"@example.com, "jo\e"@example.com, "\j\oe"@example.com, "\jo\e"@example.com, "\j\o\e"@example.com (deleting only the per-IP ipc_rl_ file between posts so every post reaches the auto-reply cap), counts the auto-replies in the mail log, then stops the server by PID and deletes the mirror. Control: _harness/out/audit12/evidence/L3-W2-G3/control1.sh posts joe@example.com 8 times the same way.

#!/bin/bash
# A12-L3-W2-G3-1 — auto-reply per-recipient cap (3/24h) vs RFC 5321 quoted local parts.
# Binds 127.0.0.1:${PORT:-10862}; private sys_temp_dir + IPC_MAIL_LOG; stops the server by PID.
set -e
cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"
PORT=${PORT:-10862}
M=$PWD/_harness/out/audit12/m/L3-W2-G3-R1; rm -rf $M; mkdir -p $M/tmp && cp -r _harness/site $M/site; cp _harness/fakemail.sh $M/
(cd $M && IPC_MAIL_LOG=$M/mail.log TMPDIR=$M/tmp nohup php -S 127.0.0.1:$PORT -t site -c ../../../../php-mail.ini -d sys_temp_dir=$M/tmp ../../../../router.php >/dev/null 2>&1 &) ; sleep 1
for a in 'joe@example.com' '"joe"@example.com' '"\joe"@example.com' '"j\oe"@example.com' '"jo\e"@example.com' '"\j\oe"@example.com' '"\jo\e"@example.com' '"\j\o\e"@example.com'; do
  rm -f $M/tmp/ipc_rl_*   # clear only the 5-per-IP limiter so all eight reach the auto-reply cap
  printf '%-24s %s\n' "$a" "$(curl -s http://127.0.0.1:$PORT/contact.php -d form_type=message -d name=x --data-urlencode "email=$a" -d subject=s -d message=hi)"
done
echo "auto-replies sent (To: not the sales address): $(grep -c '^To: [^s]' $M/mail.log)  (cap is 3 per 24 h per mailbox)"
grep '^To: [^s]' $M/mail.log
echo "auto-reply cap files: $(ls $M/tmp | grep -c '^ipc_ar_')"
P=$(ps -eo pid,comm,args | awk -v p="127.0.0.1:$PORT" '$2=="php" && index($0,p) {print $1}'); kill $P; rm -rf $M

- **Observed:** Attack run (repro1.out): all eight posts return {"ok":true}; `auto-replies sent (To: not the sales address): 8  (cap is 3 per 24 h per mailbox)`; the To: lines are joe@example.com, "joe"@example.com, "\joe"@example.com, "j\oe"@example.com, "jo\e"@example.com, "\j\oe"@example.com, "\jo\e"@example.com, "\j\o\e"@example.com; `auto-reply cap files: 8` (one cap key per spelling). Control run (control1.out): the same address 8 times gives `auto-replies sent ...: 3` and `auto-reply cap files: 1`, so the cap works only while the spelling is unchanged. PHP 8.3.6 `filter_var(..., FILTER_VALIDATE_EMAIL)` accepts every quoted form (measured with php -r). Each form is the same mailbox under RFC 5322 §3.2.4 (the quotes and a backslash before an ordinary character are not part of the address), and there is no limit on how many such spellings exist. [UNVERIFIED: that a real receiving server (Gmail, Microsoft 365, the host's own MTA) delivers each quoted spelling to joe's inbox; no outbound mail may be sent from this audit (§4 S5/S6), so only the hand-off to sendmail was measured.]

auto-replies sent (To: not the sales address): 8  (cap is 3 per 24 h per mailbox)

To: "joe"@example.com

To: "jo\e"@example.com
To: "\j\oe"@example.com
To: "\jo\e"@example.com
To: "\j\o\e"@example.com
auto-reply cap files: 8
Terminated
--- control1.out ---

- **Expected:** ipc_ar_cap_key() promises to key the cap on the MAILBOX, not the string that was typed (contact.php:483). The key has to be the address with RFC 5322 quoting removed (quotes stripped, backslash-escapes resolved), or quoted local parts refused for the auto-reply, so any spelling of one mailbox shares one cap of 3 per 24 h (DEPLOY_READINESS_v2 4.15, 4.15b).
- **Consequence:** The per-recipient cap is the control that stops a stranger from using IPC's form to send repeated mail, under IPC's domain and its SPF/DKIM, to a third party (4.15). With a fresh quoted spelling per post it no longer bounds anything: the only limit left is the per-IP 5-per-10-minutes limiter, i.e. up to 720 confirmation emails a day to one victim from one IPv4 address, against a promised 3. The control fails silently: nothing on the dashboard or in the inquiry log flags it, each submission also reaches the sales inbox as a 'lead', and complaints from the victim land on IPC's sending reputation. The reply body is already neutralised (A-5.1/A-6.3), so the harm is volume and reputation, not phishing content; hence Medium, not High.

WHATS_LEFT-history.md 4.15/4.15b at :127 and :158), _harness/AUDIT10-REPORT.md, _harness/AUDIT11-REPORT.md and _harness/out/audit12/findings/*.json for 'quoted local', 'local part', 'ipc_ar_cap_key', 'auto-reply cap', 'googlemail'. audit5.md:411 refutes header injection via a quoted local part with a comma (one address, no extra recipient); it does not consider the cap key. 4.15b normalised Gmail plus- and dot-addressing only. A12-L3-02 (gmail.com vs googlemail.com) is a different mechanism with a bounded effect (6 instead of 3, Gmail only); this one works on every domain and is unbounded. Not a re-wording of either.

<a id="a12-l4-01-w5-1"></a>
#### A12-L4-01-W5-1 — Medium · code · L4

**If the server's disk is nearly full, restoring a backup tells Rick "the state from just before this restore was backed up too, so you can undo" when no such backup was written, so the version he replaced is gone**

- **Rows:** GAP-0170
- **Where:** `admin/backups.php:88` · `admin/backups.php:204` · `admin/backups.php:39` · `admin/config.php:958` · `admin/config.php:1404`
- **Reproduce:** As root, from the repo root: bash _harness/out/audit12/A12-L4-01-W5-1.repro.sh 10012 (any free port >= 10000). It copies _harness/site to a private mirror with _harness/pristine data, serves it, mounts a 2 MB tmpfs over the mirror's data/ (data copied in), drives the real admin: (1) Page Content, add one FAQ entry with a marker and a long answer, Save (Rick's latest work; this writes one backup of the previous state); (2) fills data/ so the free space holds the smaller restored file but not a copy of the current one; (3) Backups, "Restore This Version" on that backup (the same POST the button sends). It prints the button's confirm text, the success message, which backups hold the marker state, then repeats everything with free disk as the control, unmounts and deletes the mirror. Output: _harness/out/audit12/A12-L4-01-W5-1.repro.out.
- **Observed:** Nearly full (free 49152 bytes, current content.json 54963, restore target 42204): confirm "...? The current version is backed up first, so this can be undone."; restore HTTP 200, "✅ Page Content restored to how it was at ... (The state from just before this restore was backed up too, so you can undo.)"; content.json now 42049 bytes without the marker; new content backups from the restore: []; backups holding the marker state: []; audit line "Restored Page Content from content.backup....json". Control (free disk): same message, new backup content.backup....json written and it holds the marker state. Code: the restore closures call save_*() (backups.php:28/34/39), which call backup_before_write() as a bare statement (config.php:1404 and the two siblings) and go on writing when copy() fails and it returns null (config.php:958); backups.php:88 appends the "backed up too" sentence unconditionally.
- **Expected:** backups.php promises twice (the confirm and the success message) that the current version is backed up first, and the L4 charter says every change can be undone. When the pre-restore copy cannot be made, the restore should not overwrite the only copy of the current state while saying it can be undone: refuse, or restore and say plainly that this restore cannot itself be undone.
- **Consequence:** Rick restores an older version to look at it or to undo a mistake, trusting the explicit "you can undo" message; the version he replaced, including every edit since the previous backup, exists nowhere, and Backups offers only older states. Needs a disk-full (quota) or unwritable-backup condition, so a degraded control with a false signal on a secondary path rather than loss on a normal action: Medium. Same root cause as A12-L4-05-2 (ordinary saves); this is the Backups-restore path, which A12-L4-05-2 does not measure, and here the page states the undo exists.

<a id="a12-l4-05-2"></a>
#### A12-L4-05-2 — Medium · code · L4

**If the server's disk is nearly full, a Page Content save that deletes things still goes through and says "Content saved", but no backup of the previous version is made, so Rick cannot undo it from Backups**

- **Rows:** GAP-0130
- **Where:** `admin/config.php:958` · `admin/config.php:1404` · `admin/config.php:1106` · `admin/config.php:1080` · `admin/config.php:894` · `admin/content.php:1134`
- **Reproduce:** As root, from the repo root: (1) cp -r _harness/site /tmp/m405 ; (2) php -S 127.0.0.1:<port> -t /tmp/m405 -c _harness/php-mail.ini _harness/router.php & ; (3) bash _harness/out/audit12/A12-L4-05-2.repro.sh <port> /tmp/m405 . The script checks the server serves that mirror, mounts a 2 MB tmpfs over /tmp/m405/data and copies the data in, then drives the real admin with Playwright (A12-L4-05-2.drive.js): sign in, Page Content, add one FAQ question MARKER-<n>, Save; fill data/ until 40960 bytes are free (enough for the smaller post-delete file, not for a copy of the current 42 KB file); Page Content, remove every FAQ row, Save; then lists new content backups and which backups hold the MARKER state, and unmounts. Control: on a fresh mirror without the tmpfs, node _harness/out/audit12/A12-L4-05-2.drive.js <port> <mirror> 'true'.
- **Observed:** _harness/out/audit12/A12-L4-05-2.repro.out: 'free bytes on data/: 40960; content.json size: 42370' / 'save 2 (remove all FAQ): ✅ Content saved. The website will reflect the changes within ~60 seconds. | url /admin/content.php?saved=1' / 'faq rows on disk now: 0' / 'new content backups from save 2: []' / 'backups holding the marker state: []' / audit line 'Updated: FAQ / Resources' / Backups page mentions a failed backup: false. Control (_harness/out/audit12/A12-L4-05-2.control.out): 'new content backups from save 2: ["content.backup.20261009-134733.json"]' and that backup holds the marker state. Code: backup_before_write() returns null when copy() fails (config.php:958) and all three save_*() helpers call it as a bare statement and go on to json_write_atomic() (1080, 1106, 1404); the comment at 893-894 records that no caller looks at the result.
- **Expected:** CLAUDE.md: 'Every save routes through backup_before_write()'; the L4 charter: every change can be undone. When the pre-edit copy cannot be made, the save should not overwrite the only remaining copy of the current state without telling the owner (refuse, or save and warn that this change cannot be undone from Backups).
- **Consequence:** On a host near its disk quota (shared hosting), Rick's deletion is published and reported as saved, while the version he just replaced - including any edit made since the previous backup - exists nowhere; the Backups page offers only an older state, so the most recent work is lost with no warning. Same path for Business Details and every catalog save (add, edit, delete, photo/PDF upload). Needs a disk-full or unwritable-backup condition, so a degraded control without a signal rather than loss on a normal action.
- **Not in prior:** Grepped WHATS_LEFT.md, plans/GUARDRAILS.md, _harness/AUDIT10-REPORT.md, _harness/AUDIT11-REPORT.md, audit-runs/audit*.md, audit-runs/audit-2026-09-27.md for 'disk full', 'quota', 'backup.*fail', 'backup_before_write': only audit9-ledger E078 'done' (no failure-path check) and audit5's unrelated admin_password_write backup wording. A12-L13-W1-R2-2-1 is about nodupbackups not guarding the no-op/missing-file clause, not this path; GAP-0130 itself was routed from L13 W1 as an oob line, not a finding.
- **Verification:** reproduce: confirmed · refute: confirmed · severity: confirmed (Medium)

<a id="a12-l4-05-w5-2"></a>
#### A12-L4-05-W5-2 — Medium · code · L4

**When the inquiry log reaches its 16 MB limit and two or more contact-form submissions arrive in the same second, the archive holding every earlier inquiry can be overwritten by the new, nearly empty file, so the Inquiries list loses its whole history with no warning**

- **Rows:** GAP-0309
- **Where:** `public/contact.php:144` · `public/contact.php:145` · `audit-runs/audit5.md:378` · `audit-runs/WHATS_LEFT-history.md:4888`
- **Reproduce:** From the repo root: bash _harness/out/audit12/A12-L4-05-W5-2.repro.sh 80 8 . For each trial it makes a temp root with admin/inquiries.jsonl pre-filled past 16 MB (74,948 numbered 'orig' lines), then starts 8 PHP CLI processes that each run public/contact.php's own ipc_log_inquiry() — race.php extracts the function and the two define()s from contact.php verbatim at run time and points __DIR__ at the temp root — all released at the same microtime via time_sleep_until(); it then counts the 'orig' lines and the 8 new lines across inquiries*.jsonl and prints LOSS when any is missing. Control in the same run: the trials that print 'ok' (archive 16,777,242 bytes kept).
- **Observed:** _harness/out/audit12/A12-L4-05-W5-2.repro.out (PHP 8.3.6, 2026-10-11): 'trials with lost leads: 3 / 80', e.g. 'trial 51: LOSS orig 74948 kept 0 | new leads 8/8 | files inquiries-2026-10-11-055136.jsonl:51 inquiries.jsonl:357' — the 16 MB archive replaced by a 51-byte file. Earlier runs (_harness/out/audit12/L4-05/w5/race.out): 1/20 with 8 processes, 0/20 with 2; plus 1/3 in a first probe — 5 losses in 133 eight-way trials. Every process returned true (no 'log failed' line), so contact.php clears the failure marker and nothing reaches the dashboard. Mechanism: the size check and rename run outside the flock taken later (contact.php:160); process A renames the full log to inquiries-<second>.jsonl and appends to a fresh inquiries.jsonl, then process B (which had also seen >= 16 MB) renames that fresh file onto the same second-granular name, and rename() replaces the archive.
- **Expected:** Rotation must never destroy an archive: the check-and-rename belongs under the same lock as the append (re-checking the size after taking it), or the archive name must be unique. The inquiries log is the record the admin tells Rick to trust when an email does not arrive (contact.php:110-117, A-7.4 comment).
- **Consequence:** Every inquiry recorded before the rotation — years of leads at 16 MB — disappears from admin Inquiries, silently. The notification emails already sent are unaffected, which is why this is not a lead-path Blocker; the trigger needs concurrent submissions at the one moment the log crosses 16 MB (measured only with 8 simultaneous; 0/20 with 2), e.g. a spam burst. [UNVERIFIED over HTTP: measured on contact.php's function in CLI processes, not through php -S/Apache, because php -S serves one request at a time.]
- **Not in prior:** audit5 A-5.25 (audit-runs/audit5.md:378) named this in one clause; its recorded fix (WHATS_LEFT-history.md:4888) addressed only the disk growth, and audit-2026-09-27.md:147 'already known' lists only 'Rotated logs are never deleted' for A-5.25. Grepped WHATS_LEFT.md (Open + Settled), plans/GUARDRAILS.md, AUDIT10/11 reports for 'rotat', 'clobber', 'same-second': no fix, decline or settle of the clobber, and no measurement until now. Raised here with the first measured reproduction; GAP-0309 itself came from L15-18 as an [UNVERIFIED] oob line.
- **Verification:** reproduce: confirmed · refute: confirmed · severity: confirmed (Medium)

C (MTA takes 10 s, only the PHP worker killed at 5 s): http=000; inquiries.jsonl +0; mail log 1 — the email went, the Inquiries record did not. D (MTA takes 10 s, no kill): http=200; inquiries +1; mail 2 — so the row is lost only because the request ended while mail() was still running. _harness/out/audit12/A12-L4-W2-G4-1.repro.out.

In case C he gets the email but the Inquiries list and the unread badge he is told to rely on miss it. Same root cause as A12-L2-W1-G3-1 (mail() disabled -> fatal before the log), reached on a host where mail() works; one fix (log first) closes both.

#### A12-L5-W2-G2-1 — Medium · code · L5

**If site-info.json or the catalog is saved over FTP by an editor that adds a byte-order mark, the website keeps showing Rick's new details but the contact form quietly mails every lead to the old sales@ address and the sitemap drops all 42 product pages**

- **Rows:** DATA-0025
- **Where:** `public/contact.php:34` · `public/contact.php:189` · `public/sitemap.php:88` · `public/index.php:451` · `src/App.jsx:6219`
- **Reproduce:** From the repo root, with the harness mirror and pristine data present (npm run build && sh _harness/sync.sh; php and the harness Playwright available): node _harness/out/audit12/A12-L5-W2-G2-1.repro.js 10844   (any free port >= 10000). The script copies _harness/site to _harness/out/audit12/m/A12-L5-W2-G2-1/site, loads _harness/pristine data, sets site-info.json contact.email to quotes@insulationproducts.com, and serves it with php -S plus a private copy of php-mail.ini whose sendmail_path is a private capture script and whose sys_temp_dir is private (so the rate limiter is not shared). It runs two variants: 'control' (files written as plain UTF-8) and 'bom' (the same bytes with EF BB BF prepended to site-info.json and products-all.json). For each it records: the email shown and mailto links on the hydrated /contact in Chromium; the product links on /products; the To: line of the mail contact.php sends for one message-form POST; the Inquiries row; the number of ?productId= URLs in /sitemap.xml; and whether index.php's server HTML for /contact carries the new email. It then stops its server and deletes the copy. Output is printed as JSON.
- **Observed:** _harness/out/audit12/A12-L5-W2-G2-1.repro.out. control: firstBytes 7b0a20, browserShowsNewEmail true, browserMailtoNew 3, browserProductLinks 42, contact 200 {"ok":true}, mailToLines [quotes@insulationproducts.com, probe@example.com], inquiryRowsForProbe 1, sitemapProductLocs 42, serverHtmlHasNewEmail true. bom: firstBytes efbbbf, browserShowsNewEmail true, browserMailtoNew 3, browserProductLinks 42, contact 200 {"ok":true}, mailToLines [sales@insulationproducts.com, probe@example.com], inquiryRowsForProbe 1, sitemapProductLocs 0 (status 200), serverHtmlHasNewEmail false. So with the mark present the browser (fetch().json() strips a leading BOM) renders the edited email and the full catalog, while every PHP reader's json_decode() returns null: contact.php falls back to its hard-coded recipient, sitemap.php emits only the 10 static routes under a 200, and index.php fails closed to the unmodified index.html. Nothing in public/, admin/ or src/ handles a BOM (grep -rn -i 'bom\b|xEF.xBB.xBF|ufeff' over *.php/*.js/*.jsx/*.md: only a copy-scan pattern in _harness/audit10-copyscan.js).
- **Expected:** One file, one meaning: the business email the website shows is the address contact.php mails (CLAUDE.md, contact.php 'reads data/site-info.json'; L5 charter 'contact.php (recipient)'), and sitemap.php lists the catalog the site renders (sitemap.php header: 'Reading data/products-all.json per request is the only version that cannot be stale'; A-6.7 'three readers of one file, two tolerant and one not, and the intolerant one failing silently'). Either every reader strips a leading UTF-8 BOM before json_decode, or none accepts it; today the browser accepts it and all PHP readers reject it silently.
- **Consequence:** Precondition is a hand edit over FTP with an editor that writes a UTF-8 BOM [UNVERIFIED which editors do so on Rick's machine; the effect of the mark itself is measured]. Then: buyers see and use the new address on the site, but every contact-form and quote request is mailed to sales@insulationproducts.com instead of the address Rick set, with a 200 'sent' to the buyer and nothing on the owner's side saying so (the lead is still written to Admin > Inquiries, measured, which is the workaround). Search engines are silently told the site has no product pages (0 of 42 in the sitemap, 200 status), and server-rendered heads/no-JS pages revert to the shipped defaults. Wrong with a workaround on the lead path, plus silent SEO loss: Medium.
- **Not in prior:** grepped WHATS_LEFT.md, plans/GUARDRAILS.md, audit-runs/*.md, _harness/AUDIT10-REPORT.md, _harness/AUDIT11-REPORT.md and every _harness/out/audit12/findings/*.json for 'BOM', 'byte order mark', 'byte-order', 'xEF', 'ufeff' — no hits outside audit10-copyscan.js's copy pattern. Differs from the already-raised L5 items (wrong-type email/phone/fax/hours fatal; social sameAs; ISO spaces; nav label types; blank confirmation; ISO year; SEO types; nav whitespace): those are per-field type/value mutations of a file every reader parses; this is a whole-file encoding the browser parses and every PHP reader rejects. Differs from audit6 A-6.7 (sitemap vs a {products:[...]} wrapper shape, fixed).

- **Rows:** ROUTE-0213, ROUTE-0214
- **Where:** `src/App.jsx:5682` · `src/App.jsx:5694` · `src/App.jsx:5895` · `src/App.jsx:4956` · http://127.0.0.1:10866/contact (390x844, contact.php held 8 s) (artifact `_harness/out/audit12/L7-W5-G3/sending-abort-2s.png`) · http://127.0.0.1:10866/contact (artifact `_harness/out/audit12/A12-L7-W5-G3-1.repro.out`)
- **Reproduce:** From the repo root: bash _harness/out/audit12/A12-L7-W5-G3-1.repro.sh 10866  (copies _harness/site to a private mirror, serves it with php -S on the given port, runs _harness/out/audit12/L7-W5-G3/sending.cjs and tabduring.cjs, stops the server by PID and deletes the mirror). The probes open /contact at 390x844 (isMobile), fill Full Name, Email and Quantity, put focus on 'Submit Quote Request →' with Tab, press Enter, and hold the /contact.php answer for 8 s (arm 1: then let it through; arm 2: then reset the connection), sampling document.activeElement, every [aria-live]/[role=status]/[role=alert] region and the submit button at 0.3, 2 and 5 s, then after the answer.
- **Observed:** Both arms, at 0.3 s, 2 s and 5 s: activeElement BODY; live regions [] (none on the page); button {text:'Sending…', disabled:true, aria-busy:null}; ariaSnapshot of the form ends `button "Sending…" [disabled]`. Focus before Enter was BUTTON 'Submit Quote Request →'. Only when the answer arrives does a role=alert region appear and take focus ('Network error. Please call 630.771.0700 …'). tabduring.out: 1 s after Enter activeElement is BODY (scrollY 1381); the next Tab goes to the Phone card link '630.771.0700' below the form. Screenshot sending-abort-2s.png (opened): sighted users see a spinner and 'Sending…' on the button. Source: both forms set `disabled={submitting}` (App.jsx:5682, :5895) and swap the label to cf.sendingLabel (:5694, :5907); the label change is in no live region, and disabling the focused button drops focus (Chromium focus fixup). Combined with A12-L11-W3-G4-1 (the submit fetch has no time limit), on a stalled connection the silence is open-ended. [UNVERIFIED — iOS VoiceOver / Android TalkBack speech was not run; no screen reader is installed here. What they say for a focused element that becomes disabled varies by engine; the absence of any live region, measured above, means none of them is told 'Sending'.]
- **Expected:** WCAG 2.2 SC 4.1.3 Status Messages (AA): a status such as 'Sending…' must be programmatically determinable without receiving focus (a role=status / aria-live region carrying it), and SC 2.4.3 Focus Order: focus should stay on the control the user activated (aria-disabled instead of disabled, or keep focus and mark the form aria-busy). The error and success paths already do this (role=alert focused at 4893; B16 success panel focused) — only the in-flight state is silent.
- **Consequence:** A blind buyer on a phone with a poor signal presses Submit and hears nothing for the whole time the request is travelling — seconds normally, indefinitely on a stalled connection (A12-L11-W3-G4-1). With the button now disabled and focus gone, there is no feedback that the tap registered; the natural reactions are to leave the page (which A12-L6-13-6 shows drops a rejection silently) or to give up. Secondary to the lead path itself (the request still goes through and the outcome is eventually announced), hence Medium.
- **Not in prior:** Grepped WHATS_LEFT.md, plans/GUARDRAILS.md, audit-runs/*.md (incl. WHATS_LEFT-history.md), _harness/AUDIT10-REPORT.md and AUDIT11-REPORT.md for 'sending', 'sendingLabel', 'spinner', 'Animation 8', 'in flight', 'aria-disabled', 'status message', '4.1.3': only hits are the spinner's reduced-motion fix (history:3153) and plan8-motion — neither about announcement or focus. Grepped all audit12 finding titles: A12-L11-W3-G4-1 is the missing time limit and the slow auto-reply (visual, robustness); A12-L6-13-6 is navigating away mid-send; A12-L7-01-W5-3 is focus after 'Submit Another'; A12-L13-14-1 / L13-21-1 are the motion test. None measures focus or announcement during the in-flight state; the fix here (live region / aria-disabled) is separate from a fetch timeout.

- **Reproduce:** From the repo root: sh _harness/out/audit12/repro/A12-L8-W4-G2-1.repro.sh <free port >= 10000>. The drive script reads the body text of /, /about, /faq, /services, /industries and /contact with the shipped site-info.json, then sets the mirror's data/site-info.json stats.feetInStock to "30 million" (the value Business Details -> Feet In Stock saves) and reads them again. Static half, no server needed: factsRewriter (src/App.jsx:6966-6976) builds two rules, lit("25 million") with flags "g" only (case-sensitive) and /(?<![\d.])25M(?=\+|\b)/g. The row pass missed this because the checks match case-sensitively: L9-12's drive1.js 'old' list has '25 million' and '25M', and _harness/adm7-facts.js:39 uses /25\s*M\b|25M\+|25 million/. A buyer sees two inventory claims, and Rick has no signal that the headline did not follow, because Help told him it would. Workaround: he also retypes Page Content -> Hero -> Headline line 1. Medium: wrong, with a workaround, on a claim a buyer reads first.

**If Rick empties Opens and Closes in Business Details (for example because IPC goes to 'by appointment'), the save succeeds but the site keeps telling search engines IPC is open Monday to Friday 08:00-17:00; emptying Open Days too leaves an hours entry with no days at all**

- **Rows:** ROUTE-0215, ROUTE-0023
- **Where:** `src/App.jsx:7767` · `src/App.jsx:7768` · `src/App.jsx:7766` · `src/App.jsx:6753` · `src/App.jsx:6639` · `admin/settings.php:191` · `admin/help.php:926` · http://127.0.0.1:10850/contact (artifact `_harness/out/audit12/A12-L10-W3-G2-1.repro.out`)
- **Reproduce:** From the repo root, with a built _harness/site, php and the harness Playwright: PORT=10850 sh _harness/out/audit12/A12-L10-W3-G2-1.repro.sh . The script copies _harness/site to _harness/out/audit12/m/A12-L10-W3-G2-1, serves it with php -S on $PORT, runs _harness/out/audit12/A12-L10-W3-G2-1.drive.js, which signs in to /admin (audit-pass-123), opens Business Details, (A) sets 'Hours (display text)' to 'By appointment - call ahead' and empties 'Opens (24h)' and 'Closes (24h)', presses Save Business Details; (B) also empties 'Open Days' and saves again. After each save it prints the stored data/site-info.json hours, the hours text on /contact, and the #ipc-structured-data JSON-LD openingHoursSpecification on /contact. It then stops the server by PID and deletes the copy. Manual equivalent: do the same in the admin and view-source the rendered /contact head (DevTools > Elements > script#ipc-structured-data).
- **Observed:** _harness/out/audit12/A12-L10-W3-G2-1.repro.out. STEP A: admin redirected to /admin/settings.php?saved=1; stored hours {"text":"By appointment - call ahead","opens":"","closes":"","days":["Monday",...,"Friday"]}; page shows 'By appointment - call ahead'; JSON-LD openingHoursSpecification {"dayOfWeek":["Monday","Tuesday","Wednesday","Thursday","Friday"],"opens":"08:00","closes":"17:00"}. STEP B: stored days []; JSON-LD {"dayOfWeek":[],"opens":"08:00","closes":"17:00"}. Cause: settings.php accepts and stores an empty Opens/Closes (settings.php:191 validates only a non-empty value), mergeSiteInfo drops the empty string because hours.opens/hours.closes are not in SITE_CLEARABLE (App.jsx:6753) and falls back to SITE_DEFAULTS 08:00/17:00 (App.jsx:6639), and StructuredData emits them unconditionally (App.jsx:7766-7768). With the shipped data every one of the 141 JSON-LD blocks on 11 routes and 42 products validates against the schema.org vocabulary (types, property domains, value ranges; _harness/out/audit12/L10-W3-G2/validate.js over ld.jsonl: 'total issues 0 blocks 141'), so this appears only once the owner edits the hours.
- **Expected:** L10 charter: crawler-facing data must be true (PLAN-12 §6 L10, 'JSON-LD ... and that it is true'). Help (help.php:926) tells Rick these three boxes ARE the opening hours search engines read; an emptied box should withdraw the claim, as it already does for fax, slogan, short name and the ISO certificate (SITE_CLEARABLE, the NB4 rule the same StructuredData comment cites: an absent value is better than a wrong one). With Opens, Closes or Open Days empty the openingHoursSpecification should be left out rather than filled from the shipped defaults or emitted with an empty dayOfWeek.
- **Consequence:** Search engines and map listings that read the site's LocalBusiness data are told IPC keeps Mon-Fri 8am-5pm hours that Rick removed, while the site itself says something else; a buyer relying on the search listing calls or visits outside real hours. Rick gets 'saved', sees the boxes empty, and has no signal that the old hours are still published. Secondary path, owner action needed to trigger, workaround is to type real times instead of clearing: Medium ('a control that degrades without a signal').
- **Not in prior:** Grepped WHATS_LEFT.md, plans/GUARDRAILS.md, audit-runs/*.md (incl. WHATS_LEFT-history.md), _harness/AUDIT10-REPORT.md, _harness/AUDIT11-REPORT.md and every _harness/out/audit12/findings/*.json for openingHours, dayOfWeek, hours.opens, hours_opens, 08:00/17:00: the only hit is audit9.md:1767 (Step 7), which checked opens/closes/dayOfWeek EQUAL site-info.json with the shipped data only. ADM-13 (settings.php comment) added the format check, not clearing. Not invariant 4 being simplified: the remedy is the existing SITE_CLEARABLE mechanism (or omitting the node), which invariant 4 itself provides for. Distinct from the six L10 items already raised (CT title, og:image:alt, family breadcrumb, uppercase scheme, empty FAQPage, empty product description).

With the bundle reset: / visibleTextLen=0 at every sample 1-15 s, prerenderInDom=true, prerenderDisplay=none, prerenderTextLen=512; /products?productId=CC visibleTextLen=0 throughout, prerender 958 chars hidden; /contact visibleTextLen=0 throughout, prerender 430 chars hidden. No buyer harm, no data loss, workaround exists → Medium.

<a id="a12-l12-07-1"></a>
#### A12-L12-07-1 — Medium · doc · L12

**The admin README (and the root README) tell whoever deploys to set the catalog files to 666 if 644 will not save, but the file's own permission never matters to a save: 666 does not fix 'Failed to save', and it leaves the live catalog world-writable on a shared host**

- **Rows:** DOC-0155
- **Where:** `admin/README.md:171` · `admin/README.md:425` · `README.md:175` · `admin/config.php:715` · `admin/config.php:724`
- **Reproduce:** As root, from the repo root, on Linux with php-cli and a www-data user:
  sh _harness/out/audit12/A12-L12-07-1.repro.sh
The script extracts admin/config.php's json_write_atomic() verbatim (every save_products/save_site_info/save_content goes through it), and runs it as www-data (the PHP user) against a copy of data/products-all.json in a root-owned folder (the FTP account), in four states: folder 755 or 777 x file 644 or 666. It writes only under /var/tmp and deletes it.
- **Observed:** _harness/out/audit12/A12-L12-07-1.repro.out:
  folder not writable by PHP, file 644        -> SAVE FAILED
  folder not writable by PHP, file 666 (doc)  -> SAVE FAILED   resulting file: 666 root
  folder writable by PHP, file 644            -> SAVE OK
  folder writable by PHP, file 666 (doc)      -> SAVE OK       resulting file: 666 www-data
The file mode never changes the outcome: a save writes <file>.<pid>-<n>.tmp into data/ and rename()s it over the target (config.php:715-725), which needs only the FOLDER to be writable. The 666 is then carried onto every later save by the chmod at config.php:724, so the catalog stays world-writable.
- **Expected:** One answer, and the one that works: data/ must be writable by PHP (755/775, or the host runs PHP as the account user - GO-LIVE.md B3), and the JSON files stay 644. admin/help.php and the dashboard banner already give the folder as the fix (audit 9 A-9.B2-14 #4 noted the three answers; its fix only reordered them '644-first', keeping 666).
- **Consequence:** On deploy day or when Rick reports 'Failed to save', the operator following the table or the Troubleshooting row chmods the JSON files 666, sees the save still fail, and loses time before reaching the real fix (the folder or the PHP user). If the folder is later fixed, the files keep 666 forever (carried across saves), so on Network Solutions shared hosting any other account's process can rewrite the live catalog, Business Details or Page Content. Rework plus a degraded control, no data loss: Medium.
- **Not in prior:** Grepped WHATS_LEFT.md, plans/GUARDRAILS.md §7-7.3, audit-runs/*.md, _harness/AUDIT10/11-REPORT.md and _harness/out/audit12/findings for '666'. Only hit: audit9.md:1072 (A-9.B2-14 #4), which called it 'the most permissive' of three answers and was closed by putting 644 first. That record never measured whether 666 can work; this one shows, by running the shipped write path, that it cannot (new dated evidence, 2026-10-10). No AUDIT-12 finding mentions it.
- **Verification:** reproduce: confirmed · refute: confirmed · severity: confirmed (Medium)

#### A12-L12-W5-G2-1 — Medium · doc · L12

**The first-deploy rollback (put the / to /site/ redirect back) does not bring the old site back when the deploy failed with a whole-site 500, because the new public_html/.htaccess also governs public_html/site/. Visitors are redirected straight into the same 500.**

- **Rows:** DOC-0050, DOC-0026, DOC-0049
- **Where:** `GO-LIVE.md:285` · `GO-LIVE.md:521` · `GO-LIVE.md:502` · `public/.htaccess:9` · http://127.0.0.1:10851/site/ (artifact `_harness/out/audit12/repro/A12-L12-W5-G2-1.repro.out`)
- **Reproduce:** From the repo root, with apache2 and libapache2-mod-php installed and dist/ built (npm run build): sh _harness/out/audit12/repro/A12-L12-W5-G2-1.repro.sh 10851 . The script builds a private public_html under _harness/out/audit12/m/A12-L12-W5-G2-1 holding the new site from dist/ and data/. Beside it, it puts a stub predecessor in public_html/site/, shaped like the one measured in audit-runs/live-triage-2026-09-15.md §2: index.html, assets/index-OLD.js and data/products-all.json. The vhost carries the restored redirect 'RedirectMatch 302 ^/$ /site/'. The script then runs Apache 2.4 + mod_php on 127.0.0.1:10851 with X-Forwarded-Proto: https and requests /, /site/, /site/assets/index-OLD.js and /site/data/products-all.json in five states. R0: before B2.4, no public_html/.htaccess, mod_access_compat absent. R1: after a full B2 with mod_access_compat present. R2: as R1 but mod_access_compat absent, the GO-LIVE 'Every URL ... answers 500' row. R3: R2 plus a public_html/site/.htaccess of its own. R4: mod_access_compat present, but the host's AllowOverride refuses FollowSymLinks (A12-L12-16-1 case C). It stops Apache and deletes the copy.
- **Observed:** _harness/out/audit12/repro/A12-L12-W5-G2-1.repro.out. In every state, / gives 302 to /site/. R0, with no new .htaccess yet: /site/, its bundle and its catalog all 200. R1, the normal case: all 200, so the rollback works when Apache accepts the .htaccess. R2: /site/, /site/assets/index-OLD.js and /site/data/products-all.json all 500. R3, with the predecessor's own .htaccess: still all 500. R4: all 500. The error log gives 6 x "Invalid command 'Order'" and 3 x 'Option FollowSymLinks not allowed here'. Apache reads public_html/.htaccess for every request below public_html, /site/ included. So whatever makes that file fatal for the new site makes it fatal for the predecessor too, and putting the redirect back only moves visitors from one 500 to another. GO-LIVE says nothing about this: line 285 and lines 520-522 present the redirect as the whole first-deploy rollback, and line 502 calls the mod_access_compat case a 'Host action' with no interim step.
- **Expected:** PLAN-12 §6 L12: every runbook step works as written. The first-deploy rollback has to say that, when the deploy is being backed out over a whole-site 500 (or any fault in public_html/.htaccess), the new public_html/.htaccess must also be removed or renamed before or with putting the redirect back. Otherwise /site/ answers 500 too. The 'Every URL ... answers 500' row should point to that rollback while the host action is pending.
- **Consequence:** On the first deploy, if the host lacks mod_access_compat (the runbook's own documented whole-site-500 case) or refuses FollowSymLinks, Keagan follows the documented back-out, restores the redirect, and the old site is down as well. The company then has no working website at all until the host ticket is resolved or someone works out that the .htaccess has to go. This happens only on a failed first deploy and has a workaround (delete public_html/.htaccess), and no data is lost: Medium.
- **Not in prior:** Grepped WHATS_LEFT.md, plans/GUARDRAILS.md, audit-runs/audit-2026-09-27.md (NEW-V4-1, NEW-V4-8, NEW-N3-7), audit-runs/live-triage-2026-09-15.md, audit-runs/WHATS_LEFT-history.md, _harness/AUDIT10-REPORT.md, _harness/AUDIT11-REPORT.md and every _harness/out/audit12/findings/*.json for 'rollback', '/site/', 'inherit', 'site/.htaccess'. A12-L1-W5-G2-1 covers the re-deploy rollback (index.html only; index.php/contact.php not restored), not the first-deploy redirect path. A12-L12-16-1 covers the FollowSymLinks 500 and its wrong troubleshooting row, not what it does to /site/. A12-L12-W4-G5's 500 window covers B2.4 to B2.9 with index.html absent. No source checks whether the /site/ fallback survives the new root .htaccess. Not raised before.
- **Verification:** reproduce: confirmed · refute: confirmed · severity: confirmed (Medium)

- **Observed:** _harness/out/audit12/A12-L13-06-W5-1.repro.out: the suite's only opacity check is line 125 (skips opacity '0' only); backdrop.js mentions opacity 0 times.
