The suite: 'plan8-contrast 34/35 neutral combinations meet WCAG AA', exit 0 (evidence/L13-06-W5/p8-verdict.txt), and its record row for the chip is 'rgb(55, 65, 81) on rgb(255,255,255) ratio 10.31 pass true' (60 instances in p8-report.txt line 196). axe-core and L7 measure the same span at 3.77:1 (A12-L7-01-2).
- **Expected:** plan8-contrast.js says it sweeps 'EVERY element that paints its own text' and fails 'anything under threshold' (lines 17-18). The ink it scores must include the opacity of the element and its ancestors (multiply alpha by the product of computed opacity up the tree), as its own B10 note demands for rgba alpha. Otherwise CSS opacity is an unguarded way to make text unreadable.

#### A12-L13-W1-G2-2 — Medium · harness · L13

**The audit plan tells every agent to serve its private test site with php-mail.ini, but that file finds the fake mail program only from _harness/site, so on every private copy the contact form answers "The mail server could not send your message" (500) and logs the lead as not sent, which looks exactly like a broken lead path**

- **Rows:** FILE-0155, FILE-0119
- **Where:** `_harness/php-mail.ini:18` · `plans/PLAN-12-full-project-audit.md:251` · `plans/PLAN-12-full-project-audit.md:987` · `_harness/fakemail.sh:10`
- **Reproduce:** From the repo root at f9d3089, with a synced mirror (npm run build && sh _harness/sync.sh):
1. M=_harness/out/audit12/m/probe; cp -r _harness/site $M
2. Run the PLAN-12 §5.3 command exactly as written: php -S 127.0.0.1:10852 -t $M -c _harness/php-mail.ini _harness/router.php > $M.log 2>&1 &
3. curl -s -w " %{http_code}\n" -H "Accept: application/json" -H "Referer: http://127.0.0.1:10852/contact" -X POST http://127.0.0.1:10852/contact.php --data-urlencode form_type=message --data-urlencode name="Probe Person" --data-urlencode email=probe@example.com --data-urlencode subject=General --data-urlencode message="hello from audit probe"
4. tail -1 $M/admin/inquiries.jsonl ; grep fakemail $M.log
5. Control, on the same mirror, changing only the sendmail path to an absolute one: IPC_MAIL_LOG=$PWD/$M.mail.log php -S 127.0.0.1:10853 -t $M -c _harness/php-mail.ini -d sendmail_path=$PWD/_harness/fakemail.sh _harness/router.php &   then repeat step 3 against :10853 and run: grep -c ===MESSAGE=== $M.mail.log
6. Stop both servers by PID (ps -eo pid,comm,args; comm == php and port 10852/10853), then rm -rf $M $M.*
- **Observed:** Step 3 on :10852 returned HTTP 500 with the body {"ok":false,"error":"The mail server could not send your message. Please call 630.771.0700 or email sales@insulationproducts.com directly."}. The server log shows `sh: 1: ../fakemail.sh: not found` and then `[500]: POST /contact.php`. The new inquiries.jsonl row ends "sent":false. The control on :10853 (absolute sendmail_path, nothing else changed) returned {"ok":true} with a 200, and its mail log holds 2 messages: the notification and the auto-reply. The cause is that php -S runs with its working directory at the docroot. The relative "../fakemail.sh" in php-mail.ini therefore resolves to _harness/ only when the docroot is _harness/site. With the §5.3 docroot _harness/out/audit12/m/<label>, ".." is _harness/out/audit12/m/, which has no fakemail.sh. PLAN-12 §11, the environment-artifact table, lists fakemail only as a Windows limitation, and §5.3 gives no override. A second problem remains even with the path fixed: fakemail.sh line 10 writes to the shared /tmp/ipc-harness-mail.log unless IPC_MAIL_LOG is set. §5.3 does not set it, so the private servers and the sweep's :8123 would share one mail log. Earlier agents in this audit noticed the problem and quietly added `-d sendmail_path=` (for example, the reproduce text in findings/L13-W1-G1.json), so the workaround exists only inside individual agents' runs. Both servers were stopped by PID and the mirror copy deleted. The md5 of git status --porcelain was unchanged (d41d8cd9...).
- **Expected:** PLAN-12 §5.3 is the one command every agent uses to stand up a site. The L4 lead-path check (§6: "both forms → the mail log (IPC_MAIL_LOG) and" the Inquiries row) depends on mail() succeeding. Run as written, the command should give a working capturing sendmail and a private mail log. Either php-mail.ini's sendmail_path should stop depending on how deep the docroot sits, or §5.3 should pass -d sendmail_path=<abs>/_harness/fakemail.sh with a per-agent IPC_MAIL_LOG, and §11 should list the artifact together with that control.
- **Consequence:** This harms the audit, not the site. Any finder or verifier that follows §5.3 literally and tests the contact or RFQ form gets the exact signature of a lead-path Blocker (§9.2: "the lead path fails (email and Inquiries row)"): a 500, the "could not send" message, and an Inquiries row marked not sent. The only evidence that this is the test setup sits in a server log the agent may never open, so the default reading is a site defect. At best that costs a refute or tiebreak round. At worst it puts a false Blocker in the launch verdict. The shared default mail log also lets agents and the sweep read each other's messages in their mail assertions. Medium: the audit's own procedure produces wrong results, and the workaround is undocumented.
- **Not in prior:** I grepped WHATS_LEFT.md, audit-runs/*.md (including WHATS_LEFT-history.md), _harness/AUDIT10-REPORT.md, AUDIT11-REPORT.md and plans/GUARDRAILS.md for fakemail and sendmail_path. The hits cover two other things. One is the Windows/POSIX limitation (GUARDRAILS 248 and 442, PLAN-12 §11). The other is WHATS_LEFT-history 3983-4005, a different defect: GUARDRAILS named php-extra.ini, which has no sendmail_path at all, for :8123; it was fixed in 0d5b953. None of them covers the correct ini breaking because of docroot depth on the private mirrors PLAN-12 §5.3 prescribes. I also grepped _harness/out/audit12/findings and verdicts: no finding raises it, and agents only worked around it. It is not on this lens's already-raised list.
- **Verification:** reproduce: confirmed · refute: confirmed · severity: confirmed (Medium)

It (1) greps every _harness/*.js|*.php|*.sh for 'set_password', the field auth.php requires before it acts on a reset (auth.php:85); (2) on a private copy of the mirror with config.local.php removed and ALLOW-PASSWORD-RESET created, walks GO-LIVE B4 by HTTP (_harness/out/audit12/findings/A12-L13-W5-G4-1.dayone.cjs: GET /admin/, POST the Set Admin Password form, check 302, config.local.php created as PHP, flag gone, dashboard signed in, new password signs in from a fresh browser) and runs a private copy of lowsA1-sec (the only sweep suite that opens the reset screen) on port 10893; (3) repeats on mutant A (admin_password_write()'s create-file branch drops its '<?php' line) and mutant B (auth.php's reset handler no longer fires on submit). Ports 10892/10893; mirrors are deleted at the end.
- **Observed:** Census: the only harness file naming set_password is _harness/lowsA1-sec.js:213/218, and only as a regex for the form's presence; no harness file POSTs it, so nothing reaches auth.php:85-104 or admin_password_write()'s create-file branch (config.php:164-174, the branch taken only when config.local.php does not yet exist, i.e. day one). Output (_harness/out/audit12/findings/A12-L13-W5-G4-1.repro.out; re-run identically at f2152f4 in A12-L13-W5-G4-1.repro.rerun.out): shipped code: dayone 7/7, lowsA1-sec 18/18. Mutant A: dayone 4/7 ('FAIL B4.3: config.local.php was created and is a PHP file', 'FAIL B4.3: the dashboard opens signed in, no hash on the page', 'FAIL day 2: the new password signs in from a fresh browser (got 200 )'), lowsA1-sec 18/18. Mutant B: dayone 2/7 (Set Password answers 200, no config.local.php, flag stays, nobody signed in), lowsA1-sec 18/18. The suites that change a password (plan5b-pwthrottle, sec4-sessionforge) go through password.php with config.local.php already present, and the harness writes its own credential with setpw.php, which has its own copy of the create-file code. audit9-logic-admin C26 (not in the sweep) only GETs auth.php. Other sweep suites were not re-run under the mutants; that they cannot reach these branches is from the census (no POST of set_password anywhere in _harness outside out/ and site/) [UNVERIFIED by full-sweep mutation — sweep owns ports 8123-8139].

- **Where:** `WHATS_LEFT.md:63` · `audit-runs/WHATS_LEFT-history.md:7633` · `audit-runs/WHATS_LEFT-history.md:7649` · `audit-runs/WHATS_LEFT-history.md:7613` · `audit-runs/WHATS_LEFT-history.md:7616` · `src/App.jsx:9182` · `src/App.jsx:9183` · `_harness/plan8-contrast.js:114`
- **Reproduce:** From the repo root at f9d3089.

3. Read the cell code: sed -n 9171,9188p src/App.jsx  -- each spec-table header <th> has ONE solid background (var(--brand-primary) or var(--brand-accent-2)), not a gradient, and its text is var(--brand-header-ink), which is solved for the two-stop page-header gradient.
4. In the browser: cp -r _harness/site _harness/out/audit12/m/X ; php -S 127.0.0.1:<free port >=10000> -t _harness/out/audit12/m/X -c _harness/php-mail.ini _harness/router.php ; then node _harness/out/audit12/evidence/L14-W1-G4/specth.js http://127.0.0.1:<port> CC IP12GA CT  (for every product: pass all 42 ids from data/products-all.json). The script opens /products?productId=<id> at 1440x900 and, for every <th> whose computed background is rgb(17,158,200), prints its computed colour, size/weight, the measured ratio, and the ratio #141414 would give on the same computed background.
5. Stop the server by PID (ps -eo pid,comm,args; comm == php and your port) and delete the copy.
- **Observed:** Step 1: '#ffffff on #119ec8 3.11 | on #005da3 6.79' ; '#141414 on #119ec8 5.92 | on #005da3 2.71' ; 'inkFor(#119ec8) = #141414 | inkFor([#005da3,#119ec8]) = #ffffff'. So the '2.72:1 dark ink' that §1as records 'at the light end of the header gradient (#119EC8)' is the dark ink on the OTHER end (#005da3, 2.71); on #119EC8 dark ink is 5.92:1 and passes AA. Step 4 (all 42 products, saved as _harness/out/audit12/evidence/L14-W1-G4/specth-all.txt): 72 <th> cells on 36 product pages, every one 'fg rgb(255,255,255) on rgb(17,158,200) = 3.11:1' at 12px/600, and '#141414 on it = 5.92:1' for every one; --brand-header-ink computes to #ffffff and --brand-accent-2 to #119ec8. Example lines: 'CC "A" 12px/600 fg rgb(255,255,255) on rgb(17,158,200) = 3.11:1 | #141414 on it = 5.92:1'; 'CT "I. D.\nMin.-Max" ... = 3.11:1 | #141414 on it = 5.92:1'. For the page-header gradient itself the recorded conclusion still holds (white fails on the #119EC8 end at 3.11, dark fails on the #005da3 end at 2.71, so no single ink spans both); the conclusion does not hold for the spec-table cells, which sit on one solid colour each.
- **Expected:** The Keagan decision of 2026-10-05 (history §1as, line 7611-7616) already approved exactly this kind of change: small text in a brand context 'may use a slightly darker or lighter shade ... enough to reach WCAG AA on the surface it actually sits on', and it lists `spec-table-subheader-contrast` among the items it covers. The surface each accent-2 heading actually sits on is solid #119EC8, where the site's own inkFor() picks #141414 at 5.92:1 -- a derived ink, so it re-derives on a repalette, which answers §2c's 'hardcoding would be overridden' objection. The spec-table half was escalated as 'a surface, not a text colour' and then deferred alongside the page header ('keep the header as it is') on a wrong number. WHATS_LEFT's deferred row and its 'do not re-propose without new evidence' therefore hold a fix that needs no header change and was already in scope; the record should state the measured 5.92:1 and separate the spec table from the page-header decision, for Keagan to re-decide.
- **Consequence:** A buyer reading a product's spec table sees 72 column headings across 36 of the 42 product pages (dimension letters such as A/B/C, 'Wall', 'I. D. Min.-Max') in white 12px text on pale blue at 3.11:1, below WCAG AA -- the spec-grade data he came for. Because the record says no text colour can fix it and marks it do-not-reopen, the next session will not touch it, and plan8-contrast keeps it as its one allowed exemption. Not High: the headings are readable for most sighted users and nothing is lost; it is a wrong reason holding an accessibility defect open on a secondary element.
- **Not in prior:** Grepped WHATS_LEFT.md (Open and Settled tables), plans/GUARDRAILS.md §7-7.3, CLAUDE.md invariants, history §1at and §1as/§2c, audit-runs/audit5-9.md, audit-2026-09-27.md, _harness/AUDIT10-REPORT.md and AUDIT11-REPORT.md for 'spec-table-subheader', 'sub-header', '2.72', '5.92', 'dark ink', 'EXEMPT_BRAND_SURFACE'. The item itself is recorded as deferred (WHATS_LEFT:63) -- this finding does not re-propose the header redesign; it is new dated evidence (measured 2026-10-08) that the reason recorded for deferring the spec-table half is false. Not a re-wording of the already-raised '§1as has no before/after picture' (that is about a missing artifact, not the measurement) nor of A12-L13-13-2 (that is plan8-contrast's exemption being a free slot -- a harness defect; this is the decision's premise). No prior audit12 finding under findings/ mentions 2.72 or 5.92.

#### A12-L14-W5-G2-1 — Medium · doc · L14

**If the old site's / to /site/ redirect is a rewrite rule in a .htaccess above public_html (one of the two places the runbook says to look), the new site's .htaccess silently switches it off at upload step 4, and the documented first-deploy rollback, putting that redirect back, then does nothing: visitors stay on the new site, broken or not**

- **Rows:** RECORD-0014, DOC-0050, DOC-0026, DOC-0022
- **Where:** `GO-LIVE.md:149` · `GO-LIVE.md:285` · `GO-LIVE.md:521` · `public/.htaccess:15`
- **Reproduce:** From the repo root, on a machine with /usr/sbin/apache2, mod_php and a built dist/: bash _harness/out/audit12/findings/A12-L14-W5-G2-1.repro.sh 10853 . It builds home/public_html under _harness/out/audit12/m/L14-W5-G2, puts a stand-in predecessor at public_html/site/, writes the redirect as 'RewriteEngine On / RewriteRule ^public_html/?$ /site/ [R=302,L]' in home/.htaccess (above public_html, AllowOverride All as on shared hosting), starts a private Apache 2.4 on 127.0.0.1:10853, then lays down B2 steps 1-4 (assets, index.php, the shipped public/.htaccess), then data/ and index.html, and probes /, /site/, /products at each stage; controls: the same with public_html/.htaccess removed, and the redirect written as mod_alias RedirectMatch in the same place. It stops Apache with -k stop and deletes its tree.
- **Observed:** _harness/out/audit12/findings/A12-L14-W5-G2-1.repro.out: S0 (predecessor only): '/ -> 302 .../site/' (the STEP 0b state). S1 (B2 steps 1-4, B2.0 NOT done, redirect still in home/.htaccess): '/ -> 500 | The site is being updated' — the redirect is gone without anyone removing it. S2 (deploy finished, redirect still there): '/ -> 200' new shell. S3 (the rollback state GO-LIVE:285 and :520-522 describe — the redirect present in home/.htaccess): '/ -> 200' new shell, no redirect. Control 1 (public_html/.htaccess moved away): '/ -> 302 .../site/' again, so the parent rule is valid and it is the child .htaccess that cancels it. Control 2 (same place, 'RedirectMatch 302 ^/$ /site/'): '/ -> 302' with the new .htaccess present, so the mod_alias form survives. public/.htaccess:15 is 'RewriteEngine On' and the file has no RewriteOptions line ('grep RewriteOptions public/.htaccess' -> nothing); Apache does not apply a parent directory's mod_rewrite rules to a directory whose own .htaccess turns the engine on. Where the live redirect actually lives is [UNVERIFIED — no request to the live host beyond C's STEP 0 (step0.txt shows only '302 Found location: http://www.insulationproducts.com/site/'), and the triage could not see the config]. If it is in the Network Solutions panel or written as mod_alias, the rollback works (control 2; A12-L12-W5-G2-1's R1 measured the host-level form). <a id="a12-l15-19-1"></a>
#### A12-L15-19-1 — Medium · code · L15

**The contact form's clean-up of its rate-limit files only ever looks at the first 500 files in the server's temp folder, so on a host whose temp folder is busy (session files, other sites) the old files are never removed and keep piling up — the exact problem the clean-up was added to stop**

- **Rows:** DECL-0220
- **Where:** `public/contact.php:632` · `public/contact.php:633` · `public/contact.php:634`
- **Reproduce:** D=$(mktemp -d) && TMPDIR=$D php -r '$s=file_get_contents("public/contact.php"); preg_match("/function ipc_prune_limiter_files.*?\n}\n/s",$s,$m); eval($m[0]); $d=sys_get_temp_dir(); for($i=0;$i<2000;$i++) touch("$d/sess_".md5("o$i")); for($i=0;$i<200;$i++){$f="$d/ipc_rl_".md5("ip$i").".json"; touch($f, time()-3*86400);} for($i=0;$i<25000;$i++) ipc_prune_limiter_files(time()); echo count(glob("$d/ipc_rl_*")), " of 200 three-day-old limiter files left after ~1000 sweeps\n";'; rm -rf $D   # run from the repo root. Control: delete the first for-loop (no unrelated files) and the same command prints 0 of 200.
- **Observed:** Measured 2026-10-09, PHP 8.3.6, ext4 temp dir: with 2000 unrelated files beside 200 stale (3-day-old) ipc_rl_ files, 25,000 calls of the shipped ipc_prune_limiter_files() (~1000 sweeps at its 1-in-25 rate) left "153 of 200" stale limiter files; 3000 calls also left 153, i.e. the residue is permanent, not slow. Control with no unrelated files: "0 of 200 left". With 400 unrelated files: 0 left (the window advances as limiter files are deleted). The 500 budget is decremented for EVERY readdir() entry, not per limiter file, and readdir order on a hashed directory is stable, so each sweep re-reads the same leading 500 entries; once those are non-limiter files nothing past them is ever examined.
- **Expected:** A-5.9 (audit-runs/audit5.md:318, High, SHIPPED 2026-08-18 per WHATS_LEFT-history §1r) requires stale ipc_rl_/ipc_ar_/ipc_lk_ files to be pruned so that one file per distinct visitor IP does not accumulate "forever, in the same directory as PHP's session files". The bound has to cap work without pinning the sweep to a fixed slice of the directory (e.g. count only examined limiter entries, or resume from a varying offset).
- **Consequence:** On a shared host whose sys_get_temp_dir() holds more than ~500 entries ahead of the limiter files (other accounts' or the host's session files — the scenario A-5.9 itself names), every distinct visitor IP leaves an ipc_rl_ file plus an ipc_lk_ lock file that is never removed, so the unauthenticated inode-growth path A-5.9 closed is open again there, silently; inode exhaustion is the condition under which both contact-form limiters fail open. No lead is lost by this alone. Whether the production temp dir is that crowded is [UNVERIFIED — Network Solutions temp dir not observable from here; S5 forbids probing the live host].
- **Not in prior:** Grepped WHATS_LEFT.md, plans/GUARDRAILS.md, audit-runs/audit5.md..audit9.md, audit-runs/audit-2026-09-27.md, audit-runs/WHATS_LEFT-history.md, _harness/AUDIT10-REPORT.md, _harness/AUDIT11-REPORT.md for "budget", "prune", "ipc_rl_", "readdir", "A-5.9": A-5.9 is recorded as SHIPPED with pruning; no source examines the 500-entry budget's effect on a crowded temp dir. The only harness check (_harness/audit5-high.js:175) is a source regex for the function name. Sibling AUDIT-12 finding A12-L13-W1-G1-1 is about that suite being textual, not about this behaviour. Incomplete fix of A-5.9 (High) in the shared-temp scenario it described, not a regression of a measured-working state.
- **Verification:** reproduce: confirmed · refute: confirmed · severity: confirmed (Medium)

<a id="a12-l2-05-1"></a>
#### A12-L2-05-1 — Low · code · L2

**Two lines in the site's main Apache file are guarded by the wrong module check, so on a host missing mod_setenvif (or carrying mod_deflate without mod_filter) every page answers 500 instead of quietly losing a header, which is what the file's own comment promises**

- **Rows:** HTACCESS-0078, HTACCESS-0097
- **Where:** `public/.htaccess:45` · `public/.htaccess:71` · `public/.htaccess:133` · `public/.htaccess:135` · `public/.htaccess:165` · `public/.htaccess:166`
- **Reproduce:** Scripted (real Apache 2.4.58 + mod_ssl + mod_php, fresh docroot copied from _harness/site, every repo .htaccess copied verbatim; ports 10009/10010): from the repo root `NO_SETENVIF=1 OUT=v-nosetenvif.txt node _harness/out/audit12/L2-05/apache-pub.js; grep -c ' -> 500' _harness/out/audit12/L2-05/v-nosetenvif.txt` and `NO_FILTER=1 OUT=v-nofilter.txt node _harness/out/audit12/L2-05/apache-pub.js; grep -c ' -> 500' _harness/out/audit12/L2-05/v-nofilter.txt`. Controls: `NO_SETENVIF=1 PUB_DROP=71 OUT=v-nosetenvif-drop71.txt ...` and `NO_FILTER=1 PUB_DROP=166-168 OUT=v-nofilter-drop166.txt ...`. By hand on any Apache 2.4: 1) docroot = npm run build output with public/.htaccess at its root; 2) load mod_rewrite, mod_headers, mod_php but comment out `LoadModule setenvif_module`; 3) `curl -sk -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' https://<host>/` -> 500 and error.log says Invalid command 'SetEnvIf'. Same with mod_deflate loaded and mod_filter not loaded -> Invalid command 'AddOutputFilterByType'.
- **Observed:** _harness/out/audit12/L2-05/v-nosetenvif.txt: 169 of the probe's requests -> 500, error.log `public_html/.htaccess: Invalid command 'SetEnvIf', perhaps misspelled or defined by a module not included in the server configuration`. With line 71 also removed (v-nosetenvif-drop71.txt) the public tree serves normally (the six remaining 500s are all /admin/*, from admin/.htaccess:47's identical unguarded line), and line 136's SetEnvIf, which IS inside <IfModule mod_setenvif.c>, fails safe exactly as its comment says (assets get max-age=3600, not immutable). v-nofilter.txt: 169 -> 500, `Invalid command 'AddOutputFilterByType'`; with lines 166-168 removed: 0 -> 500. Baseline (all modules, apache-pub.out.txt): 0 -> 500.
- **Expected:** Every optional-module directive in public/.htaccess sits inside an <IfModule> for the module that defines it, as lines 133-137 state is the design ("If mod_setenvif is absent the variable is never set and nothing is long-cached — the safe direction to fail in"). Line 71 (SetEnvIf, mod_setenvif) is inside <IfModule mod_headers.c> only; lines 166-168 (AddOutputFilterByType, provided by mod_filter in Apache 2.4) are inside <IfModule mod_deflate.c> only.
- **Consequence:** On a host whose Apache lacks mod_setenvif, or has mod_deflate without mod_filter, the whole public site (and, for SetEnvIf, the admin via admin/.htaccess:47) returns 500 on every request instead of merely losing HSTS-behind-proxy or compression. Both modules are on in stock Apache builds and the Network Solutions module list is [UNVERIFIED — host not reachable from this audit, S5], so the likelihood is low; it is a latent mismatch between the guards and the file's stated fail-safe design, not an observed outage.
- **Not in prior:** grepped WHATS_LEFT.md, plans/GUARDRAILS.md, audit-runs/*.md (incl. WHATS_LEFT-history.md, audit6.md, audit-2026-09-27.md), _harness/AUDIT10-REPORT.md, _harness/AUDIT11-REPORT.md, CLAUDE.md for 'SetEnvIf', 'setenvif', 'mod_filter', 'AddOutputFilterByType', 'IfModule'. Hits: PUB-1/NEW-V3-1 (which SetEnvIf matches, HTTPS vs X-Forwarded-Proto), A-6.4 (which MIME types the deflate list names), WHATS_LEFT-history.md:1019 ('All three depend on mod_setenvif / mod_headers being present' - says the features depend on the modules, not that their absence 500s the site). None covers the guard naming the wrong module.
- **Verification:** reproduce: confirmed · refute: confirmed

<a id="a12-l2-w1-g2-2"></a>
#### A12-L2-W1-G2-2 — Low · code · L2

**The main Apache file says that if the host cannot run PHP the site still serves its normal page, but measured on Apache with PHP not running, every page (the home page, every product page, the sitemap) sends the raw PHP source of index.php instead**

- **Rows:** HTACCESS-0068
- **Where:** `public/.htaccess:13` · `public/.htaccess:14` · `public/.htaccess:120` · https://127.0.0.1:10842/ (artifact `_harness/out/audit12/L2-W1-G2/r2/probe-nophp.txt`)
- **Reproduce:** Scripted, real Apache 2.4 + mod_ssl, the PHP module NOT loaded (the conf's <FilesMatch \.php$> SetHandler line is kept, as on a host whose PHP handler is broken). From the repo root: 1) cp -r _harness/site _harness/out/audit12/m/L2-W1-G2  2) NOPHP=1 HTTP=10841 HTTPS=10842 node _harness/out/audit12/L2-W1-G2/probe-nophp.js (prints the four lines, then 'FAIL harness: NOPHP done', which is the script's deliberate stop)  3) rm -rf _harness/out/audit12/m/L2-W1-G2. By hand: any Apache 2.4 without mod_php/proxy_fcgi, docroot = npm run build output, AllowOverride All; curl -sk https://<host>/ | head -c 40 ; curl -sk https://<host>/products | head -c 40.
- **Observed:** Re-run 2026-10-09 (r2/probe-nophp.txt), Apache/2.4.58, php_module not loaded: '/ 200 CT=- first40="<?php\n/**\n * The front controller for ev" phpSource=true len=33961'; '/products 200 CT=- ... phpSource=true len=33961'; '/sitemap.xml 200 CT=- first40="<?php\n/**\n * The sitemap, generated from" phpSource=true len=8446'; only '/index.html 200 CT=text/html' is the shell. DirectoryIndex picks the first name that EXISTS, not the first that runs, and the catch-all rewrites every route to index.php, so index.html is reached only by its own URL. Control (same script, PHP loaded, r2/probe-new.txt): /products 200 text/html; charset=UTF-8 with the rendered title.
- **Expected:** The comment's promise holds, or the comment says what really happens. Nothing in .htaccess can detect a missing PHP handler in general (an <IfModule> test sees mod_php but not PHP-FPM), so the honest fix is the comment: without PHP the public site is down (raw source, no Content-Type), not degraded to the static shell. Rule: L2 charter, every .htaccess directive does what its comment says.
- **Consequence:** Only on a host whose PHP stops running for public_html (a broken handler after a host-side PHP change). There the comment tells a maintainer the public site is safe and only the head tags degrade, when in fact every visitor gets a 34 kB page of PHP source (no secrets in it; the repository is public) and no website; the contact form and admin are down too. A maintainer reading the comment would look elsewhere first.
- **Not in prior:** Grepped WHATS_LEFT.md, plans/GUARDRAILS.md, audit-runs/*.md, audit-runs/WHATS_LEFT-history.md, _harness/AUDIT10-REPORT.md, _harness/AUDIT11-REPORT.md and _harness/out/audit12/findings/*.json for 'DirectoryIndex', 'stays second', 'static shell', 'cannot run PHP' and 'no PHP': no record measures the no-PHP fallback A-5.10 claims. Distinct from A12-L2-05-1 (IfModule guards for mod_setenvif/mod_filter, a 500) — this is a host without a working PHP handler and a 200 with source.
- **Verification:** reproduce: confirmed · refute: confirmed

Without @, the same call prints 'PHP Warning: Zend OPcache API is restricted by "restrict_api" configuration directive' and returns bool(false) (php -d opcache.enable_cli=1 -d opcache.restrict_api=/nonexistent-dir -r 'var_dump(opcache_invalidate(__FILE__, true));'). The return value is not checked, and both success messages are based on re-reading the file (config.php:203-205), not on what the running PHP will use. Production host opcache settings: [UNVERIFIED - not measurable without a request to the live host (S5)]. Per-process opcode caches under mod_fcgid/CGI (the handler .user.ini says Network Solutions uses) would give the same symptom with the API open, because the invalidation reaches only the worker that served the POST: [UNVERIFIED - no php-cgi/FPM binary].
- **Expected:** The password the owner just set is the one that signs in, as the Password page and admin/README.md:418 ('so it applies at once') promise, and the documented FTP recovery (GO-LIVE B4, auth.php set_password) restores access. If the cache cannot be invalidated, the page should say so (e.g. 'saved, but may take up to N minutes on this server') instead of a plain success. The code comment at config.php:194-198 already names the validate_timestamps=Off case as one it means to handle.
- **Consequence:** Rick, on the documented 'Rotate it at Sign in -> Password' step (GO-LIVE B4 note) or after a suspected leak, is told the change worked. At next sign-in his new password is 'Incorrect' and repeated tries walk him into the login cool-off; meanwhile the OLD password, the one he wanted to retire, still opens the admin. With validate_timestamps=Off this lasts until the host restarts PHP, and the FTP reset does not help either, so a Rick who no longer remembers the old password is locked out with no self-service way back. Only on a host that sets opcache.restrict_api (or runs per-process caches) - not known to apply to the production host - so Low by the same rule as A12-L2-W1-G3-1 (a host setting not known to apply); a reviewer who knows the host sets it should treat it as a silently failing security control (High).
- **Not in prior:** Grepped WHATS_LEFT.md, plans/GUARDRAILS.md, CLAUDE.md, audit-runs/*.md incl. WHATS_LEFT-history.md, _harness/AUDIT10-REPORT.md, _harness/AUDIT11-REPORT.md and _harness/out/audit12/findings/*.json for opcache, restrict_api, validate_timestamps, revalidate_freq, opcache_invalidate. Hits: history T1.2 (the opcache_invalidate call was added) and line 943 ('recovered password signs in after opcache revalidation', measured with the API open); history:2034 (harness ini revalidate_freq=0); audit-2026-09-27 NEW-V4-7 (opcache masking a 600/root-owned config.local.php - a permissions issue, not this). None measures a host where opcache_invalidate() is refused. **A new admin password containing a hidden NUL character crashes the Change Password and reset screens with a PHP fatal error on PHP 8, and on the host's PHP 7.4 it would be accepted but cut off at that character.**

PHP 7.4 behaviour (password_hash silently hashing only the bytes before the NUL, so 'a\0bbbbbbbbbbbb' passes the 12-character rule and stores a 1-character password) is [UNVERIFIED - no PHP 7.4 binary in this container; inferred from crypt_blowfish reading the key as a C string].

**The admin's "file not on the server" check promises to refuse any address containing "..", but a URL-encoded "%2e%2e" slips past it, so a signed-in admin can ask the server whether any file anywhere on the host exists (for example /etc/passwd)**

- **Rows:** DECL-0261
- **Where:** `admin/config.php:1230` · `admin/config.php:1237` · `admin/config.php:1238` · `admin/config.php:2378` · `admin/settings.php:348`
- **Reproduce:** 1. cp -r _harness/site _harness/out/audit12/m/repro && cd _harness/out/audit12/m/repro
2. php -r 'require "admin/config.php"; $up=str_repeat("%2e%2e/",12); foreach (["/../etc/passwd", "/{$up}etc/passwd", "/{$up}etc/nope"] as $u) echo $u, " missing=", var_export(site_file_missing($u), true), "\n";'
   -> the literal '..' form says missing=true (blocked as documented); the encoded form says missing=false for /etc/passwd and missing=true for /etc/nope, i.e. it stat()s an arbitrary path outside the web root and reports the answer.
3. Over HTTP (php -S 127.0.0.1:<port> -t _harness/out/audit12/m/repro -c _harness/php-mail.ini _harness/router.php; sign in at /admin/auth.php with the mirror password): set data/site-info.json catalogPdfUrl to "/" + 12x"%2e%2e/" + "etc/passwd" (the Business Details form accepts it: link_url_problem() returns '' for any value starting with '/') and GET /admin/settings.php -> no "Not on the server" box; set it to .../etc/nope -> the box appears listing "Catalog PDF URL". 4. rm -rf _harness/out/audit12/m/repro
- **Observed:** CLI on a mirror copy (PHP 8.3.6): "/%2e%2e/x12/etc/passwd => missing=false", "/%2e%2e/x12/etc/nope => missing=true", "/../%2e%2e/.../etc/passwd => missing=true". HTTP: settings.php with the passwd value -> grep -c "Not on the server" = 0; with the nope value -> 1, item "Catalog PDF URL". Artifacts: _harness/out/audit12/m/L3-04/s1.html, s2.html; probe script _harness/out/audit12/m/L3-04/sfm.php.
- **Expected:** The function's own contract (config.php:1230) — any ".." counts as missing — should hold after decoding: the '..' test belongs after rawurldecode(), or the decoded path should be realpath()-contained under the site root, matching the CLAUDE.md security posture ("basename() + realpath() containment on every read/write/delete").
- **Consequence:** Only a signed-in admin (the owner, behind CSRF) can use it, and it yields one bit — exists / does not exist — for any path the PHP user can stat, shown as a warning on Business Details, Page Content and product saves. No file content leaks and nothing is written. It is a containment check that does not do what its comment says, not an exposure to the public, hence Low.
- **Not in prior:** grepped WHATS_LEFT.md, plans/GUARDRAILS.md, audit-runs/*.md (incl. WHATS_LEFT-history.md), _harness/AUDIT10-REPORT.md, _harness/AUDIT11-REPORT.md and every _harness/out/audit12/findings/*.json + rows/*.jsonl for 'site_file_missing', '%2e%2e', 'rawurldecode'. Only hits: WHATS_LEFT-history.md:7333 (DI-6 introducing site_file_missing, no traversal discussion), :1147 (Apache /data/%2e%2e, a different endpoint), and sibling rows FILE-0508/FILE-0246/FILE-0248 (dev middleware, audit-log.php, backups.php — different code). Not previously reported.

<a id="a12-l3-04-w5-1"></a>
#### A12-L3-04-W5-1 — Low · code · L3

**The contact form's 5-per-10-minutes limit stops holding for one sender once their lock file is two days old: the form's clean-up deletes the lock while it is in use, and one burst from one address got 10 to 23 messages through instead of 5**

- **Rows:** GAP-0312
- **Where:** `public/contact.php:580` · `public/contact.php:581` · `public/contact.php:634` · `public/contact.php:637` · `public/contact.php:575`
- **Reproduce:** From the repo root: bash _harness/out/audit12/findings/A12-L3-04-W5-1.repro.sh 10007
(it copies _harness/site to _harness/out/audit12/m/repro-A12-L3-04-W5-1, starts php -S with PHP_CLI_SERVER_WORKERS=8 and a private sys_temp_dir on the given port, then fires 40 concurrent POSTs to /contact.php from 127.0.0.1 three times with a fresh ipc_lk_ipc_rl_<md5(127.0.0.1)>.json lock file and five times with that file touched to 3 days ago, prints how many got HTTP 200, stops its server by PID and deletes the copy). To see the mtime cause alone: touch -d '3 days ago' f; php -r '$h=fopen("f","c"); flock($h,LOCK_EX);'; stat -c %y f  -> still 3 days ago.
- **Observed:** _harness/out/audit12/findings/A12-L3-04-W5-1.repro.out: fresh lock -> 'accepted(200)=5 of 40' x3; aged lock -> 20, 14, 21, 5, 15 of 40. Earlier run (_harness/out/audit12/L3-04-W5/burst.out): fresh 5 in 6/6 bursts, aged 10,18,14,23,15,18,10,15,10,16 in 10/10. Lock mtime unchanged by fopen('c')+flock: _harness/out/audit12/L3-04-W5/g312-mtime.out. The per-recipient auto-reply cap (same lock pattern, contact.php:960-961) held at 3 in 8/8 aged bursts from 40 distinct IPs (_harness/out/audit12/L3-04-W5/burst2.out), so the measured bypass is the per-IP rate limit only.
- **Expected:** PUB-13 (audit-runs/audit-2026-09-27.md:222, FIXED 2026-09-28) made same-address requests queue on one lock so the cap of 5 holds under a multi-worker burst. That has to stay true whatever the lock file's age: the prune must not unlink a lock file that may be held (for example, skip ipc_lk_ files, or prune them only with a non-blocking flock that succeeds, or refresh the lock's mtime when it is taken).
- **Consequence:** An unauthenticated sender who made one request at least two days earlier (and before any prune cleared the old lock) can, in one concurrent burst, get roughly 2-4x the cap of sales notifications and inquiry rows through, plus one auto-reply each up to its own cap; the next burst needs another two-day wait, and nothing logs that the limit was exceeded. It is a partial regression of PUB-13, which was itself Low, and costs Rick some extra spam, not data or access; hence Low.
- **Not in prior:** Grepped WHATS_LEFT.md, plans/GUARDRAILS.md, audit-runs/*.md (incl. WHATS_LEFT-history.md), _harness/AUDIT10-REPORT.md, _harness/AUDIT11-REPORT.md and _harness/out/audit12/findings/*.json for 'ipc_lk', 'PUB-13', 'flock', 'lock file'. PUB-13 (audit-2026-09-27.md:114, :222, :469) is the pre-lock race; WHATS_LEFT-history.md:6864-6865 records the decision to give locks the ipc_lk_ prefix and prune them 'like the rest', with no note that pruning a held lock breaks it. A12-L15-19-1 is the 500-entry prune budget (files never removed), the opposite failure. Not previously reported; new dated measurement 2026-10-11.
- **Verification:** reproduce: confirmed · refute: confirmed

Low: a degraded defence-in-depth layer with no exploit on the shipped configuration. #### A12-L4-W2-G1-1 — Low · code · L4

**If the server kills an Edit-page save that renames a SKU after it has renamed the data sheet but before the catalog is written, the product's Data Sheet button goes dead; saving again says "saved successfully" and restoring a backup does not bring it back**

- **Rows:** INVARIANT-0017, ADMIN-0040
- **Where:** `admin/edit.php:217` · `admin/edit.php:244` · `admin/edit.php:247` · `admin/edit.php:273` · `admin/config.php:1257`
- **Reproduce:** From the repo root (needs strace and root ptrace; uses _harness/out/audit12/L4-W2-G1/edit-sku.js, a Playwright driver that signs in, opens Edit for a SKU, changes the SKU field and submits): bash _harness/out/audit12/A12-L4-W2-G1-1.repro.sh 10825 . The script copies _harness/site to a private mirror, serves it, attaches strace to the php server with a 30 s delay injected on the FIRST rename() syscall (which is the data-sheet rename at edit.php:217), drives Edit CC -> CC-X, freezes the server (kill -STOP) and prints disk state, kills it (kill -9, standing in for a host process kill / worker restart), restarts it, prints state, retries the same rename through the real form, then restores the newest catalog backup through backups.php and prints state again. Output captured in _harness/out/audit12/A12-L4-W2-G1-1.repro.out.
- **Observed:** 1. before: catalog CC -> /pdfs/CC.pdf; pdfs/ has CC.pdf; GET /pdfs/CC.pdf -> 200 application/pdf. 2. frozen after rename(".../pdfs/CC.pdf", ".../pdfs/CC-X.pdf") = 0: catalog still CC -> /pdfs/CC.pdf; pdfs/ has only CC-X.pdf. 3. after the process died and the server came back: same; GET /pdfs/CC.pdf -> 200 text/html (the SPA shell, i.e. not a PDF). 4. retry: flash "CC-X saved successfully" with no 'Not on the server' note; catalog CC-X -> /pdfs/CC.pdf; file still at CC-X.pdf; Data Sheet still dead. 5. Backups restore: "Product Catalog restored to how it was at 2026-10-07 11:01:13"; catalog CC -> /pdfs/CC.pdf; file still at CC-X.pdf (.pdf-renames.json has no CC.pdf entry, so restore_trashed_files() cannot move it back); Data Sheet still dead. The dashboard row for the product shows a normal 'View PDF' link; nothing in the admin flags the missing file (product_save_warnings() checks photoUrl and additionalPdfs but not pdfUrl).
- **Expected:** L4 charter: nothing Rick does can silently fail to publish, and every change can be undone. The NEW-N2-3 fix (edit.php:267-275) puts the data sheets back when save_products() RETURNS false, but the rename is committed to disk before the save and is only undone by code that runs after it, so a request that dies in between (host kills the worker, PHP fatal, restart) leaves the same state NEW-N2-3 described, and DI-1's rename record (written only after a successful save) is missing too, so the Backups undo that DI-1 exists for does not apply. Either the rename should happen after the catalog write (and be recorded before it), or the save should warn when the product's main data sheet is not on the server, as it already does for Additional PDFs.
- **Consequence:** Buyers clicking the Datasheet button for that product get the site's HTML shell instead of the PDF; Rick is told the save succeeded, his retry and his Backups restore both leave it broken, and the only repair is re-uploading the PDF on Upload PDF or renaming it over FTP. Needs a process death inside a sub-second window on a SKU rename, so rare; Low, matching the adjudicated severity of the NEW-N2-3 parent (audit-2026-09-27.md:350).
- **Not in prior:** Grepped WHATS_LEFT.md, plans/GUARDRAILS.md, audit-runs/audit*.md, audit-runs/WHATS_LEFT-history.md, _harness/AUDIT10-REPORT.md and AUDIT11-REPORT.md for NEW-N2-3, DI-1, 'interrupt', 'SIGKILL', 'kill -9', 'process dies', 'mid-request'. NEW-N2-3 (audit-2026-09-27.md:260, :350; fixed per WHATS_LEFT-history.md:6793 'The PDF rename is rolled back when the save fails') covers only a save that returns false (full quota via ulimit -f); its fix is the post-save rollback at edit.php:273, which does not run when the request dies. No prior item covers a killed request, the missing DI-1 record in that case, or pdfUrl being absent from product_save_warnings(). Not one of the three items already raised for L4 in this audit.
- **Verification:** reproduce: confirmed · refute: confirmed

For the spoken order: node _harness/out/audit12/L7-W3-G2/snap.js http://127.0.0.1:<port> 1440 <outdir> against a served mirror copy and read the line starting '- group "Certifications and standards' in home-1440.yaml.

The copy is a visual device (the source comment: 'The duplicate exists only so translateX(-50%) can wrap without a visible seam'); under prefers-reduced-motion it is not rendered (10 vs 20 asserted by plan8-motion), but nothing hides it from assistive technology when motion is allowed.

The driver signs in as audit-pass-123 and, on Business Details, tries three pairs for Phone (display) / Phone (dial link): '630.771.0800' / '630.771.0800', '(630) 771-0800' / '630-771-0800', and the unchanged '630.771.0700' / '6307710700'. It gets the same refusal: '(630.771.0700) and ... (6307710700) are different numbers'. site-info.json is unchanged each time. He types it in both boxes, as the labels invite, and is told the two numbers differ when he can see they are the same. It serves the mirror with php -S, using a private ini: php-mail.ini with sendmail_path set to a capturing script under _harness/out/audit12/L9-W5-G4r/repro2 and sys_temp_dir set to a private folder, so no other tester's rate-limit or cap files count. It then POSTs the RFQ form to /contact.php four times, all from rick.owner.test@example.com (form_type=rfq, name, email, quantity, partNumber=IP33PO, empty honeypot), counts the captured messages per To: line, prints the sent flag of each Inquiries row, greps the owner documents for any mention of a daily auto-reply limit, and stops the server by PID. The cause is public/contact.php:957-979: a cap of 3 auto-replies per recipient per 24 h (86400 s), which silently sets $autoReplyOk = false. - **Where:** `src/App.jsx:7914` · `src/App.jsx:8068` · `src/App.jsx:8073` · `public/index.php:521` · http://127.0.0.1:10873/products?productId=IP12GA (artifact `_harness/out/audit12/findings/A12-L10-W5-G3-1.repro.out`)
- **Reproduce:** From the repo root with a built _harness/site mirror: PORT=10873 sh _harness/out/audit12/findings/A12-L10-W5-G3-1.repro.sh > out.txt. It copies the mirror to _harness/out/audit12/m/repro-L10-W5-G3-1, serves it with php -S on PORT, and runs _harness/out/audit12/findings/A12-L10-W5-G3-1.drive.js (Playwright Chromium, 390x844), which opens /products?productId=IP12GA five times: unmodified; with /data/products-all.json delayed 6 s; answered with a connection reset; answered 503; never answered (stall past the 12 s abort). Each run prints the title and canonical the server sent, then title, description, canonical, og:url, og:title, og:image, robots, whether #product-ld exists and the visible h1, at 2.5 s, 5 s and 16 s. The script stops its server by PID and deletes its copy.
- **Observed:** _harness/out/audit12/findings/A12-L10-W5-G3-1.repro.out (cold run on port 10873). In all five runs the server sends title 'General Purpose Vinyl Tubing — IP12GA — IPC' and canonical https://www.insulationproducts.com/products?productId=IP12GA. Unmodified: the browser keeps that head, productLd=true. reset / 503 / stall: at 2.5 s, 5 s and 16 s the head is title 'Product Catalog — Insulation Products Corporation', description 'Browse IPC's full catalog of heat shrink tubing, sleeving, and adhesives. Filter by product family, view specs and data sheets, and request a quote.' (the /products landing page's), canonical=null, og:url=null, og:title='Product Catalog — Insulation Products Corporation', og:image=https://www.insulationproducts.com/images/og-card.jpg (not the product photo ip12ga.jpg the server sent), robots=null, productLd=false. It never recovers in the page. delay6s: the same generic head at 2.5 s and 5 s, the product head back at 16 s once the file arrives. The first attempt on port 10872 lost its php -S server mid-run (ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED, an environment artifact per §11/S10); the re-run on 10873 is the one recorded.
- **Expected:** A product URL whose correct head the server has already delivered (public/index.php, A-5.10) keeps that head while the catalog is pending or failed in the browser. PUB-2's 'pending' head (no canonical, generic title) was designed when the browser had nothing better; the server now sends the real product head, and the browser should not replace it with a weaker one. The same rule the PUB-2 suite states: an outage must not change what the product URL tells search engines.
- **Consequence:** Search engines that render JavaScript (Google) and hit a 503, reset or slow catalog fetch during their render are left with a product page whose head carries the catalog landing page's title and description (the same on all 42 product URLs), no canonical, no product photo and no Product structured data, though the raw HTML said otherwise. That render can hold the product out of rich results and blur which URL is canonical until the next crawl. Link unfurlers do not run JavaScript and are unaffected; a buyer sharing from the phone's browser share sheet in that state shares the generic title. Conditional and self-healing on recrawl, a lesser consequence than PUB-2's noindex (Medium, conditional), so Low.
- **Not in prior:** Grepped WHATS_LEFT.md, plans/GUARDRAILS.md, _harness/AUDIT10-REPORT.md, _harness/AUDIT11-REPORT.md, audit-runs/audit-2026-09-27.md and WHATS_LEFT-history.md for 'PUB-2', 'pending', 'outage': PUB-2 fixed the noindex/'Part not found' half and _harness/pub2-outage.js accepts '!h.canonical' as a pass, so this residual was accepted when no server head existed; prerender.js line 249 covers only a catalog damaged on the SERVER (both sides pending). Grepped _harness/out/audit12/findings/*.json: A12-L5-W5-G3-1 is the BODY being replaced by 'Catalog Unavailable' in the same outage (buyer-visible, L5/L11); A12-L15-17-3 is the server's head when PHP cannot read the file. Neither measures the browser removing the server's correct head (canonical, og:url, og:image, Product JSON-LD). Not in the already-raised L10 list.
- **Verification:** reproduce: confirmed · refute: confirmed

Stall variant (MTA 150 s): every sample at 3, 15, 30, 60, 90, 120 and 150 s reads `button 'Sending…' disabled, alert null`, inquiries +0 until 160 s (+1, button still 'Sending…' because the auto-reply then stalls too); no network failure fired in the browser. - **Expected:** The L11 charter: 'graceful when anything fails … each must show a message'. The buyer's confirmation should depend only on the work that decides whether the lead is safe (the sales mail and the inquiry log), not on the courtesy copy that contact.php itself calls 'best-effort only' (:940); and the form should bound its own wait the way the three data fetches do, falling back to cf.networkError (which carries the phone number) instead of an open-ended spinner.

It then runs `npx vite build`, the plan's `git checkout -- .`, `git status --porcelain` and the plan's `git worktree remove`, and finally force-removes the worktree and deletes everything it made.)

- **Consequence:** Whoever runs step M from the plan stops at step 6 with a fatal error and has to work out that --force or git clean is safe. <a id="a12-l12-16-2"></a>
#### A12-L12-16-2 — Low · code · L12

**A comment in the admin password code says a password hash written in double quotes works fine at login. For about four hashes in five it does not: PHP reads part of the hash as a variable and the hash is corrupted.**

- **Rows:** GAP-0206
- **Where:** `admin/config.php:141` · `admin/config.php:142`
- **Reproduce:** php -r '$bad=0; for($i=0;$i<200;$i++){ $h=password_hash(bin2hex(random_bytes(8)), PASSWORD_BCRYPT, ["cost"=>4]); $v=@eval("return \"".$h."\";"); if($v!==$h) $bad++; } echo "double-quoted hashes altered: $bad / 200\n";'   (it hashes random throwaway strings; no real credential is involved). Then: sed -n '140,147p' admin/config.php
- **Observed:** 'double-quoted hashes altered: 161 / 200'. After the third '$' comes the 22-character salt. When the salt begins with a letter (or underscore), PHP's double-quoted string treats '$<salt…>' as a variable, which is undefined, so that part of the hash is replaced. The comment at admin/config.php:141-142 says the opposite.
- **Expected:** The comment should be true. The code beside it handles both quote styles, and that part is correct. The comment should say a double-quoted hash is usually corrupted by interpolation (which is one more reason to accept and rewrite either style), not that it 'works perfectly at login'.
- **Consequence:** Someone maintaining the code who trusts the comment might hand-write config.local.php with double quotes. About 80% of the time the admin then shows the not-configured screen or rejects the password, and the recovery is the ALLOW-PASSWORD-RESET flow. This affects only a developer reading the comment. Rick and buyers are not affected.
- **Not in prior:** Grepped WHATS_LEFT.md, plans/GUARDRAILS.md, audit-runs/audit5.md and audit-runs/WHATS_LEFT-history.md for 'quote style', 'interpolat' and 'works perfectly'. History line 4925 records the quote-style fix and repeats 'works at login' as background, but never measures interpolation. Grepped _harness/out/audit12/findings/*.json for 'works perfectly' and 'interpolat': none. Routed from L3-02 (GAP-0206).
- **Verification:** reproduce: confirmed · refute: confirmed

<a id="a12-l13-04-3"></a>
#### A12-L13-04-3 — Low · harness · L13

**The audit workflow files a finding under "killed" when one of its verifiers simply fails to return, with no verdict against it and no tiebreak**

- **Rows:** FILE-0065, FILE-0064
- **Where:** `_harness/audit12-workflow.js:224` · `_harness/audit12-workflow.js:229` · `_harness/audit12-ledger.js:372`
- **Reproduce:** Save the script below as _harness/out/audit12/evidence/L13-04/probe-nullverifier.js (it resolves _harness/audit12-workflow.js four directories up) and run `node _harness/out/audit12/evidence/L13-04/probe-nullverifier.js` from the repo root. It loads the workflow exactly as audit12-workflow-dryrun.js does (export stripped; agent/pipeline/parallel stubbed; parallel() maps a throw to null) and feeds one High finding whose reproduce verifier throws while refute and severity return confirmed. Look at ret.killed and the verify calls.
// L13-04: what does audit12-workflow.js do with a finding whose reproduce verifier returns nothing
// (agent skipped/died -> parallel() yields null)? Same stubbing as audit12-workflow-dryrun.js.
const fs = require('fs'); const path = require('path');
const src = fs.readFileSync(path.resolve(__dirname, '../../../../audit12-workflow.js'), 'utf8');
const body = src.replace(/^export const meta/m, 'const meta');
const AsyncFunction = Object.getPrototypeOf(async () => {}).constructor;
const fn = new AsyncFunction('agent', 'pipeline', 'parallel', 'phase', 'log', 'args', 'budget', 'workflow', 'Date', 'Math', body);
const pipeline = (items, ...stages) => Promise.all(items.map(async (it, i) => { let v = it; for (const s of stages) { try { v = await s(v, it, i); } catch { return null; } } return v; }));
const parallel = (thunks) => Promise.all(thunks.map((t) => t().catch(() => null)));
const labels = [];
const agent = async (prompt, opts) => {
  const l = opts.label; labels.push(l);
  if (l.startsWith('find:')) return { batch: 'L3-01', rows: [{ id: 'ADMIN-0001', status: 'finding', evidence: 'measured xxxxxxxx', findings: ['A12-L3-01-1'] }],
    findings: [{ id: 'A12-L3-01-1', title: 'T', severity: 'High', class: 'code', lens: 'L3', rows: ['ADMIN-0001'], where: [{ file: 'a', line: 1, quote: 'q' }], reproduce: 'r', observed: 'o', expected: 'e', consequence: 'c', notInPrior: 'n' }], outOfBrief: [], ledgerGaps: [], citeExit: 0 };
  if (l === 'verify:A12-L3-01-1:reproduce') throw new Error('verifier died');           // -> null
  if (l.startsWith('verify:')) { const [, id, lens] = l.split(':'); return { findingId: id, lens, verdict: 'confirmed', severity: 'High', reason: 'r', measurement: 'm' }; }
  if (l.startsWith('gap:')) return { findings: [], method: 'm', ledgerGaps: [], citeExit: 0 };
  return { coverageOutput: '', spotAudit: [], redispatch: [], unexercised: [] };
};
fn(agent, pipeline, parallel, () => {}, () => {}, { wave: 'WT', lenses: ['L3'], batches: [{ batch: 'L3-01', lens: 'L3', ids: ['ADMIN-0001'] }] }, {}, null, Date, Math)
  .then((ret) => { console.log(JSON.stringify({ verifyCalls: labels.filter((l) => l.startsWith('verify:')), confirmed: ret.confirmed, killed: ret.killed, capped: ret.capped }, null, 1)); });

- **Observed:** Return value: confirmed: [], killed: [{"id":"A12-L3-01-1",...,"by":[]}], capped: [] — the finding is killed although no verifier voted against it; no tiebreak is dispatched (verify calls: reproduce, refute, severity only), nothing is logged or capped, and its title enters the gap-hunt "already raised" list as "[killed] T". The same applies when the refute agent or the tiebreak returns nothing (line 231: alive = !!tie && ...). --tally (audit12-ledger.js:372) would list the same finding as UNVERIFIED, so the two instruments disagree. The dryrun (23/23) has no arm for a null verifier; all five Appendix C mutations were re-applied and each went red as recorded (evidence/L13-04/mut.out.txt).
- **Expected:** A verifier that returns nothing is a cap or a blocked verification (recorded in `capped` and logged), and the finding is reported as unverified, matching --tally's survival rule — never killed with an empty "by".
- **Consequence:** During AUDIT-12 a real finding can drop into the workflow's killed list (and be shielded from re-raising by the gap hunt) because an agent hit a limit, not because it was refuted. --tally/D3 ("unverified 0") is the backstop, so the loss is caught if C reconciles against --tally. Harness hygiene on an audit instrument (PLAN-12 §9.2 Low).
- **Not in prior:** Grepped plans/PLAN-12-full-project-audit.md (Appendix C, revision log, §5.5, §10) for "null", "returned nothing", "unverified", "dies": the plan records the five dry-run mutations, none for a null verifier. No earlier audit covers audit12-* (written 2026-10-07).
- **Verification:** reproduce: confirmed · refute: confirmed

#### A12-L13-W1-G2-1 — Low · harness · L13

**The audit's citation gate accepts a citation to the finder's own untracked scratch file, to an artifact outside the repository, and to any file line at all once the entry also has a url, so 'citations pass' does not prove the cited text exists at AUDIT_HEAD**

- **Rows:** FILE-0062, FILE-0065
- **Where:** `_harness/audit12-cite.js:51` · `_harness/audit12-cite.js:56` · `_harness/audit12-cite.js:52` · `plans/PLAN-12-full-project-audit.md:934` · `_harness/audit12-workflow.js:246`
- **Reproduce:** From the repo root at f9d3089:
1. S=_harness/out/audit12/scratch/cite-probe; mkdir -p $S
2. echo 'this quote exists only in an untracked scratch file' > $S/fake.txt
3. Write $S/probe-cite.json containing four findings, each with rows ["FILE-0062"]:
   PROBE-1 where [{file:"$S/fake.txt", line:1, quote:"this quote exists only in an untracked scratch file"}]
   PROBE-2 where [{file:"_harness/site/admin/config.php", line:1, quote:"<?php"}] (control: fails only on quote length)
   PROBE-3 where [{url:"http://x/", artifact:"/etc/hostname"}]
   PROBE-4 where [{url:"http://x/", artifact:"_harness", file:"src/App.jsx", line:999999, quote:"nothing like this"}]
4. node _harness/audit12-cite.js $S/probe-cite.json; echo exit=$?
5. git check-ignore -v $S/fake.txt
6. rm -rf $S
- **Observed:** audit12-cite: 1 file(s), 4 citation(s), 1 failure(s)
  FAIL probe-cite.json PROBE-2: _harness/site/admin/config.php:1 quote missing or under 6 characters
exit=1
The single failure is the control's 5-character quote. PROBE-1 passes: it cites a file under _harness/out/ that .gitignore:79 ignores, so the file is not at AUDIT_HEAD and no fresh clone or verifier could see it. PROBE-3 passes on an artifact outside the repository (/etc/hostname), because line 52 checks only that path.resolve(ROOT, artifact) exists, not that it is inside ROOT. PROBE-4 passes on src/App.jsx:999999 with a quote that is in no file, because line 51 `continue`s past the file/line/quote checks whenever `url` is present. In the same tree, `_harness/audit12-workflow.js:244-253` never runs the gate. It only logs and flags whatever `citeExit` the finder reports about itself (`citeFailed: !!r.citeExit`), so the gate's permissive answer is the only citation check before verification. Measured on today's findings: none of the 405 `where` entries in _harness/out/audit12/findings/*.json cites an untracked path or pairs url with file, so no current finding is affected (node scan in method). Re-run 2026-10-09 by this agent: identical output (4 citations, 1 failure, PROBE-2 only, exit=1).
- **Expected:** PLAN-12 §9.1 requires `where` to be quoted "(at AUDIT_HEAD)", and §9.4 says the gate checks that "the file exists inside the repo". The gate's own header says it exists because "A model-written `file:line` is a claim like any other". A file citation should be limited to paths tracked at AUDIT_HEAD (git ls-files). An artifact should resolve inside the repository's _harness/out/audit12/. An entry carrying both url and file should have its file checked as well.
- **Consequence:** This affects the audit's own record, not the site or Rick. A finder's citation can point at text the finder wrote into its own gitignored scratch file, or at a file and line that do not exist, and still pass the gate with exit 0, which the workflow then reports as citeFailed:false. Such a citation fails only later, when a verifier or the W5 fresh-clone re-verify happens to read it. That costs a round trip and puts false 'citations pass' lines in the record. There is no damage to the site, so the severity is Low (harness hygiene).
- **Not in prior:** Grepped WHATS_LEFT.md, plans/GUARDRAILS.md, audit-runs/*.md, _harness/AUDIT10-REPORT.md and AUDIT11-REPORT.md for 'audit12-cite': the only hit is _harness/README.md:20, which lists it as an instrument. The already-raised list for this lens has one audit-workflow item ('files a finding under killed when a verifier fails to return'), which concerns verify(), not the citation gate. Row FILE-0062 was closed 'done … No dead code' after running the gate only on a finding file that passed. It never fed the gate a citation that should fail, so this negative case is new.
- **Verification:** reproduce: confirmed · refute: confirmed

**The test that guards 'a save that changes nothing still succeeds' only checks half of that rule: if someone made a missing backup count as a failed save again, the test would stay green while the admin refused to recreate a missing Business Details file**

- **Rows:** INVARIANT-0016
- **Where:** `CLAUDE.md:278` · `_harness/README.md:117` · `admin/config.php:1106` · `admin/config.php:902` · `_harness/nodupbackups.js:106`
- **Reproduce:** From the repo root with a populated _harness/site (npm run build && sh _harness/sync.sh && php _harness/setpw.php): `sh _harness/out/audit12/L13-W1-R2-2/repro.sh` (PORT=10001 by default; it copies the mirror to _harness/out/audit12/m/, points private copies of nodupbackups.js/audit9-fixes.js at it, and deletes the copy at the end). By hand: (1) cp -r _harness/site <M>/site; cp _harness/pristine/*.json <M>/site/data/; serve it with php -S 127.0.0.1:<P> -t <M>/site -c _harness/php-mail.ini _harness/router.php; (2) copy _harness/nodupbackups.js with BASE -> :<P> and DATA -> <M>/site/data; (3) in <M>/site/admin/config.php save_site_info(), change `    backup_before_write($path, 'site-info');` to `    if (backup_before_write($path, 'site-info') === null) return false;` (the 'null means failure' regression the invariant forbids); (4) run the nodupbackups copy; (5) run `php _harness/out/audit12/L13-W1-R2-2/save-missing.php <M>/site/admin/config.php` (deletes SITE_INFO_JSON in the mirror, then calls save_site_info()) on the mutant and on the original.
- **Observed:** Mutant (16c): `nodupbackups 10/10`, exit 0 (_harness/out/audit12/L13-W1-R2-2/mut-16c-nodup.txt; repro.out line 'nodupbackups 10/10'). Same mutant, file absent: `save_site_info on a missing file returned false; file exists now: false`; original code: `returned true; file exists now: true` (repro.out). Control: the first clause IS guarded — mutant 16a (no-op branch returns false) gives nodupbackups 7/10 ('FAIL unchanged save redirected as a success (settings.php)'), mutant 16b (no json_write_needed skip) gives 5/10 ('FAIL unchanged save wrote no backup (1 -> 2)') — mut-16a-nodup.txt, mut-16b-nodup.txt. grep -n backup_before_write _harness/*.js finds only a comment in nodupbackups.js; no suite deletes a data file before a save.

CLAUDE.md invariant 16 has two clauses; _harness/README.md:117 names nodupbackups.js as its guard, so breaking either clause should turn a named suite red. backup_before_write() returns null exactly when there is nothing to back up (config.php:902, file absent) or the copy failed (config.php:958); a check that saves onto an absent file would catch the regression.
- **Consequence:** Nobody is harmed today — the code is correct (all three save_*() ignore the return). The harm is latent: a refactor that reinstates 'null = failure' ships green, and then an owner whose content.json or site-info.json is missing (first deploy without it, or a host that lost it) gets 'could not save' on every attempt and cannot recreate the file from the dashboard. Medium: a control that degrades without a signal; not High because the suite does fail for the invariant's main clause.

<a id="a12-l14-01-w5-3"></a>
#### A12-L14-01-W5-3 — Low · harness · L14

**One claims-register script contains a raw NUL byte, so git, GitHub and grep treat it as a binary file: its diffs are never shown and searches over the harness silently skip it**

- **Rows:** GAP-0135, GAP-0144, GAP-0148
- **Where:** `_harness/claims-extract.js:141` · `_harness/claims-extract.js:150`
- **Reproduce:** From the repo root:
1. git show 53410b3 --stat | grep claims-extract   -> "_harness/claims-extract.js | Bin 0 -> 7324 bytes"
2. git ls-files --eol _harness/claims-*.js   -> claims-extract.js is "i/-text w/-text"; the other four are "i/lf w/lf".
3. node -e 'const b=require("fs").readFileSync("_harness/claims-extract.js");console.log(b.indexOf(0))'   -> 6563, inside line 141's template literal `${r.file}<NUL>${r.text}` (grep -a -n "const k = " _harness/claims-extract.js | cat -v shows ^@).
4. grep -n writeFile _harness/claims-*.js | wc -l   -> 3, and stderr 'binary file matches'; grep -a -n writeFile _harness/claims-*.js | wc -l -> 4. git grep -n claims-extract prints 'Binary file _harness/claims-extract.js matches' instead of lines.
5. node --check _harness/claims-extract.js   -> exits 0 (the script itself is valid).
- **Observed:** Byte 6563 of _harness/claims-extract.js is 0x00, written as a literal in a Map key separator (line 141). Git classifies the file -text, so commit 53410b3 recorded it as "Bin 0 -> 7324 bytes" and no diff of it has ever been reviewable; plain grep reports only "binary file matches" and skips its contents (writeFileSync count 3 vs 4 with -a).
- **Expected:** A tracked JavaScript source is text: the separator can be written as the escape '\u0000' (or '\x00'), which produces the identical string at runtime without a raw control byte in the file.
- **Consequence:** Harness hygiene only: a reviewer of any future change to the register script sees 'Binary file not shown', and an audit grep over _harness (for writes, paths, ports) silently misses this file's lines. No site or owner impact.
- **Not in prior:** Grepped WHATS_LEFT.md (Open tables + Settled), plans/GUARDRAILS.md §7-§7.3, CLAUDE.md invariants, audit-runs/WHATS_LEFT-history.md (§1at), audit-runs/audit5..9.md, audit-2026-09-27.md, _harness/AUDIT10-REPORT.md, _harness/AUDIT11-REPORT.md, and every _harness/out/audit12/findings/*.json, for claims-extract, NUL, binary. Only L13-01-W5 GAP-0024 mentions claims-extract.js (its scan list), not the encoding.
- **Verification:** reproduce: confirmed · refute: confirmed

<a id="a12-l15-w2-g4-1"></a>
#### A12-L15-W2-G4-1 — Low · code · L15

**A buyer who sends a quote request and then clicks to another page while the email is still going out is pulled back to the contact page a few seconds later, so the page they chose is replaced by 'Quote Request Received' without them doing anything**

- **Rows:** DECL-0059, DECL-0004
- **Where:** `src/App.jsx:5010` · `src/App.jsx:5024` · `src/App.jsx:4975` · `src/App.jsx:78`
- **Reproduce:** 1. cp -r _harness/site _harness/out/audit12/m/L15-W2-G4 ; php -S 127.0.0.1:10894 -t _harness/out/audit12/m/L15-W2-G4 -c _harness/php-mail.ini _harness/router.php &
2. node _harness/out/audit12/L15-W2-G4/navaway.js http://127.0.0.1:10894 3000
   (1440x900: load /contact?part=IP12GA, fill every required field of the quote form, click Submit; Playwright holds the POST to /contact.php for 3 s, as a slow mail() on a shared host does, then answers {"ok":true}; 300 ms after Submit the visitor clicks the visible navbar link to /products; the script prints the URL and h1 at +0.5 s and after the answer, and the history length.)
3. Control for the failure path: node _harness/out/audit12/L15-W2-G4/navaway.js http://127.0.0.1:10894 3000 fail (the answer is {"ok":false,...}).
4. Open _harness/out/audit12/L15-W2-G4/navaway.png.
- **Observed:** navaway.out: 'just after nav  : /products | h1: Product Catalog' then 'after response  : /contact?part=IP12GA&sent=1 | h1: Quote Request Received', confirmation visible: true, history length 4, navigations [/contact?part=IP12GA, /contact?part=IP12GA, /products, /contact?part=IP12GA&sent=1]. The screenshot (opened) shows the full 'Quote Request Received / Thank you!' page where the visitor had opened the Product Catalog. navaway-fail.out (control): the visitor stays on /products, no message of any kind, history length 3. Mechanism: the submit handler awaits the POST and then calls the setter that ContactPage got from useSearchParam("sent"); react-router 6.30.6's setSearchParams from the unmounted ContactPage navigates to '?sent=1' resolved against the pathname and query it last rendered with (/contact?part=IP12GA), and pushes it, so it overrides the visitor's own navigation.
- **Expected:** An answer that arrives after the visitor has left the contact page must not navigate. The success handler should only write ?sent=1 while the contact page is still the current page (e.g. a mounted/aborted ref or an AbortController cancelled on unmount); the visitor's own click is the last word on where they are. The comment above setSentParam (B17) says the param is 'written once, in the submit handler, by a deliberate user action' — here it is written after the user has deliberately gone elsewhere.
- **Consequence:** A buyer who submits, then (with the button still on 'Sending…') opens the catalog to keep browsing is yanked off the product page they were reading a few seconds later, and an extra history entry is pushed, so Back from the confirmation returns to /products and Back again to the form. No lead is lost and the message shown is true, so the harm is disorientation and a broken Back sequence on the main conversion path; it only occurs while contact.php is slow (two mail() calls), which other AUDIT-12 findings show does happen on shared hosting. Low.
- **Not in prior:** Grepped WHATS_LEFT.md, plans/GUARDRAILS.md, audit-runs/*.md, _harness/AUDIT10-REPORT.md, _harness/AUDIT11-REPORT.md for 'navigat* away', 'in flight', 'yank', 'pulled back', 'after unmount', 'setSentParam': the only related item is audit9 A-9.P7-2 (sent=1 shown without a submit; CLAUDE.md invariant 18), which is about a cold load and is untouched here — this is a real submit whose late answer overrides a later navigation. Also grepped _harness/out/audit12/findings/*.json for onRfqSubmit/onMsgSubmit/setSentParam and quote-request titles: none covers it; it is not in the 'already raised' list for L15.
- **Verification:** reproduce: confirmed · refute: confirmed

#### A12-L15-W2-G5-1 — Low · code · L15

**If a brand color in site-info.json is stored without its leading # (e.g. aa0000, from an FTP edit, an old backup or a crafted Business Details post, all of which the admin's own color check accepts), every page loses its navbar, page-banner and Request a Quote button backgrounds, leaving white text on a near-white page**

- **Rows:** DECL-0135, DECL-0126, DECL-0291
- **Where:** `src/App.jsx:8281` · `src/App.jsx:8293` · `admin/config.php:1903` · `admin/settings.php:160`
- **Reproduce:** From the repo root: sh _harness/out/audit12/L15-W2-G5/repro.sh (copies _harness/site to a private mirror, prints ipc_parse_hex_color() for 'aa0000' and '#a00', serves the copy on 127.0.0.1:10914, then for each of '#aa0000', 'aa0000', '#a00' writes it as theme.primaryColor and theme.darkColor into the copy's data/site-info.json, opens /about in Chromium at 1440x900 and prints the computed --brand-primary, --brand-primary-rgb, the Request a Quote button background and the page-header background; screenshots go to _harness/out/audit12/L15-W2-G5/theme-*.png; then stops the server by PID and deletes the copy). Manually: put "primaryColor": "aa0000", "darkColor": "aa0000" in data/site-info.json theme and load any page.
- **Observed:** _harness/out/audit12/A12-L15-W2-G5-1.repro.out (PHP 8.3.6, Chromium 1194, 2026-10-09): ipc_parse_hex_color('aa0000') and ('#a00') both return [170,0,0], i.e. the settings.php gate treats both as valid. '#aa0000' (control): quoteBtnBg rgb(170, 0, 0), hdrBg linear-gradient(135deg, rgb(170, 0, 0) ...). 'aa0000': --brand-primary 'aa0000', --brand-primary-rgb '170, 0, 0' (rgbOf accepts it), but quoteBtnBg rgba(0, 0, 0, 0) with quoteBtnColor rgb(255, 255, 255), hdrBg none, h1 color rgb(255, 255, 255). Screenshot _harness/out/audit12/L15-W2-G5/theme-aa0000.png (opened with Read): navbar, logo text, menu, 'Request a Quote' and the About banner heading and intro are white on the near-white page background and practically invisible. '#a00': solids follow (rgb(170,0,0)) but --brand-primary-rgb stays '0, 93, 163', so every rgba() tint and the hover shade stay the old blue while the solids turn red.
- **Expected:** One rule for what a brand color is, applied at both gates: either ThemeInjector normalises what parseHexColor/ipc_parse_hex_color accept (prefix '#', expand 3-digit) before writing --brand-* and the *-rgb triples, or the admin and the site refuse those forms. A-5.27's stated purpose for the settings.php check is that these values are 'injected verbatim into CSS custom properties on every public page'; the check passes a value that is not valid CSS.
- **Consequence:** Not reachable from the Business Details color pickers (<input type=color> always posts #rrggbb, and NEW-N2-4 makes the page re-save a normalised value). Reached by an FTP hand edit, restoring an older backup, or a crafted authenticated POST. When reached, every public page's navigation, quote button and page banners become unreadable for every visitor until someone happens to press Save in Business Details; nothing in the admin flags it (the color picker shows the normalised #aa0000 as if all were well).
- **Not in prior:** Grepped WHATS_LEFT.md, plans/GUARDRAILS.md, audit-runs/*.md, _harness/AUDIT10-REPORT.md, _harness/AUDIT11-REPORT.md for 'rgbOf', 'A-5.27', 'NEW-N2-4', 'transparent', and _harness/out/audit12/findings/*.json for 'primaryColor', 'brand-primary-rgb'. audit-2026-09-27.md:261 NEW-N2-4 (+N1-7, Low) described this exact site-side symptom ('`005da3` -> button rgba(0,0,0,0)'); WHATS_LEFT-history.md:6794 records NEW-N2-4 as fixed with the scope 'Colour inputs never show or save black for a non-#rrggbb value' - the admin half only. Measured 2026-10-09 at f9d3089 the site half is unchanged: this is the unfixed remainder of NEW-N2-4, not a regression and not a new defect class. Raised so C can decide whether the closure record should say the site half was left open; kill as duplicate if that is the ruling. AUDIT11-REPORT.md:406 mentions rgbOf only as a line-number citation.
- **Verification:** reproduce: confirmed · refute: duplicate · tiebreak: confirmed

### 6.2 Tools and environments not available

- PHP 7.4 (the host's stated minimum): only PHP 8.3.6 in the container; 7.4-only notices and deprecations are [UNVERIFIED] (static scans only).
- PHP-FPM / CGI: no binary; every handler-dependent row (`.user.ini`, `index.php` under FPM) is [UNVERIFIED]. Real Apache ran as mod_php 8.3, installed by C via apt.
- WebKit and Firefox: only Chromium is installed, so Safari/iOS and Firefox rendering is NOT-MEASURED.
- The live host: only the STEP 0 GETs (§1). Whether `/site/admin/` accepts a leaked credential is [UNVERIFIED] (A12-L3-W5-G2-2).
- Fonts: the image ships Inter; C rejected it with a fontconfig rule so DejaVu is the default, as on the plan's machine (§1).

### 6.4 Incidents that touched the evidence

- **GAP rows wiped twice** (2026-10-10 20:51Z and 2026-10-11 10:54Z): agents ran `audit12-ledger.js --check`, which regenerates `ledger.jsonl` and drops GAP rows (raised as A12-L12-13-2). C rebuilt them deterministically both times (0 mismatches). Agents that fetched GAP rows inside those windows got nothing for them.
- **Mirror contamination (W4):** one finder's repro drove another finder's port and emptied the fax number in that finder's private mirror. Its later contact/fax rows were re-checked (GAP-0658, done).
- **Deleted evidence:** C's server-restart cleanup removed two screenshot artifacts (§8); both were recaptured (GAP-0659) and the citations repointed.
- **HEAD drift:** from 2026-10-09 the branch head is `f2152f4` (the hash-literal removal). `git diff f9d3089 f2152f4 -- src public admin data` is empty, so measurements taken there apply to `f9d3089`; the §5.6 re-verify ran on a fresh clone at `f9d3089`.
- **Usage limits** interrupted W1, W3, W4 and W5 repeatedly. Every resume replayed finished agents from cache with identical prompts, so no finished work was redone.

## 7. Proposed fix plan

A proposal only — nothing here is approved. Batches are grouped by class and surface and ordered by their worst severity. "Guarding suites" are the SUITE rows the findings themselves name; "test-first" means: turn the finding's own reproduction into a failing check, watch it fail, then fix. No time estimates.

| ID | decision-needed | recommended | why | trade-off | blocked |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|

## 9. Method

Ledger generated from the repository (`audit12-ledger.js`), 15 lenses in five waves, each a Workflow run of find → verify (reproduce · refute · severity, tiebreak on disagreement) → loop-until-dry gap hunt (5-round cap) → completeness critic (3-round cap). Agents worked on private mirrors on ports 10000+; C kept the sweep servers on 8123–8139.

| Step | Lenses | Agents | Wall-clock (measured, summed over resumes) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Phase 0 + 1 | — | C | sweep 40.6 min (§1) |
| W1 | L1 L2 L13 L14 | 376 | 13.5 h |
| Step M | L13 (invariants, mutation) | 1 | 3.4 h |
| W2 | L3 L4 L5 | 242 | 5.3 h |
| W3 | L6 L7 L10 L11 | 256 (+ resume) | 5.9 h + 1.0 h + 4.4 h |
| W4 | L8 L9 L12 L15 | 377 | 3.1 h + 3.9 h |
| W5 | all 15 (cross-lens seams) | 426 | 4.5 + 3.7 + 3.8 + 3.6 + 1.8 + 3.7 + 3.3 h |
| Leftover verification | — | 19 | 0.24 h |
| §5.6 re-verify (fresh clone) | — | 1 | 0.08 h |

Agent counts are the final run's `agentCount` (resumes replay finished agents from cache, so they are not added). Cost: every wave hit the account's session or weekly usage limit at least once; per-wave token totals are in `_harness/out/audit12/W*-output.json`.
